HESCOM consumers of Athani, Bagalkot, Bailhongal, Belagavi, Bhatkal, Chikkodi, Dandeli, Gadag, Gokak, Guledgudda, Haveri, Hubballi-Dharwad, Ilkal, Indi, Jamkhandi, Karwar, Kumta, Laxmeshwar, Mahalingpur, Mudhol, Nargund, Nippani, Rabakavi-Banahatti, Ramdurg, Ranebennur, Saundatti, Savanur, Sirsi and Vijayapura will not be able to avail themselves of online services for the scheduled period.
This apart, the HESCOM portal, online bill payment services and HESCOM related services at KarnatakaOne counters will not be available for two days, the release added.

title: NHRC issues notice to Uttar Pradesh government over alleged police torture leading to death
summary: NHRC issues notice to UP govt over suicide after police torture, demands report within two weeks. Mental health helplines available.
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Friday (July 25, 2025) issued notice to the Uttar Pradesh government in the case of a death by suicide of  a person allegedly after facing physical torture by the police in Farrukhabad district.
According to the reports, the incident took place on July 15. The kin alleged that the police had called the victim to a police station following a complaint against him by his wife. He reached the police station with his father for a compromise, but he was tortured and a bribe was demanded to settle the matter.
Observing that the matter raises a serious issue of violation of human rights of the victim, the commission has issued a notice to the Director General of Police, Uttar Pradesh, calling for a detailed report on the matter, within two weeks.
(Mental health helplines across the country can be accessedhere)

title: Rain alert: Schools in parts of Hassan, Chikkamagaluru districts to remain closed today
summary: The district administrations of Hassan and Chikkamagaluru have declared holiday for schools in parts of the districts on Saturday, following the warning of heavy rains
content:
Shivamogga
The district administrations of Hassan and Chikkamagaluru have declared holiday for schools in parts of the districts on Saturday, following the warning of heavy rains.
Hassan Deputy Commissioner K.S. Lathakumari has declared a holiday for anganwadis, primary schools and high schools in Sakleshpur and Belur taluks.
Similarly, Chikkamagaluru Deputy Commissioner Meena Nagaraj has declared a holiday for schools and anganwadis in Koppa, Kalasa, Mudigere, Sringeri, and N.R. Pura taluks and Aavathi, Jagara, Vastare, Aldur and Khandya hoblis of Chikkamagaluru taluk on Saturday.
Both the Deputy Commissioners have instructed the schools to conduct special classes on the weekends or holidays to compensate for the loss of school days.
The Indian Meteorological Department has issued an orange alert for Hassan, Chikkamagaluru, and Shivamogga districts for the next two days.
Many parts of these districts received moderate to heavy rains in the 24 hours that ended at 8.30 a.m. on Friday.
Shivamogga recorded an average of 40 mm as against the normal of 22 mm on the day. The highest of 114 mm was recorded at Sulagodu in Hosanagar taluk.
Chikkamagaluru recorded an average of 26 mm of rain as against the normal of 17.
Begar village in Sringeri taluk received the highest rainfall of 100 mm in the 24 hours. Hassan received an average of 17 mm as against the normal of 8 mm. Hongadahalla in Sakleshpur taluk recorded the highest of 177 mm.
At a review meeting in Chikkamagaluru, Ms. Meena Nagaraj said that due to heavy rains in district since June 1, as many as 1,273 electricity poles had been uprooted, and Mescom had suffered a loss of ₹2.17 crore. The work to replace the damaged poles was going on.
A total of 11.49 km of State highways had been damaged, resulting in the loss ₹6.15 crore. As many as 38 houses had been damaged, and of them, nine had collapsed completely.

title: Rajnath Singh, Naidu hail successful trial of UAV-launched missile in Kurnool
summary: DRDO successfully test-fires ULPGM-V3 missile, enhancing India's drone warfare capabilities with precision and indigenously developed technology.
content:
In a remarkable push to India’s drone warfare capabilities, the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) on Friday successfully test‑fired an indigenously developed UAV‑Launched Precision‑Guided Missile (ULPGM‑V3) at the National Open Area Range (NOAR) near Palakolanu in Orvakal mandal, Kurnool district.
Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh announced the achievement on X, sharing a photograph from the test site. He lauded DRDO scientists, MSMEs, and start‑ups involved in the project, stating, “This proves India’s ability to master complex technologies and produce world‑class systems indigenously.”
The missile, designed to neutralise fixed‑wing unmanned aerial targets with high accuracy, works on a fire‑and‑forget principle and is seen as a decisive step in next‑generation combat readiness. Developed on the earlier ULPGM‑V2 platform, the V3 variant underscores India’s push for cost‑effective, precision weapons.
The NOAR test range, spread over 2,200 acres, is one of DRDO’s most advanced facilities. It has been the site of trials of cutting‑edge systems, including directed-energy weapons.
Responding to the development, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu tweeted: “It is a proud moment that our State contributes to India’s defence strength. The ULPGM‑V3 success reflects the true spirit of Aatmanirbhar Bharat.”
Officials said the weapon will significantly sharpen India’s drone combat strategy.

title: CID nabs absconding Hyderabad Cricket Association (HCA) secretary from Pune
summary: CID arrests HCA secretary for forgery and misappropriation of funds, with ongoing investigation into financial irregularities within the association.
content:
The Crime Investigation Department (CID) of Telangana on Friday arrested the absconding secretary of the Hyderabad Cricket Association (HCA) in connection with an ongoing investigation into forgery, criminal breach of trust and misappropriation of funds by the association’s office bearers.
The accused, Devaraj Ramchander, 63, was apprehended from a hotel in Pune, Maharashtra, based on reliable intelligence inputs, and subsequently brought back to Hyderabad, said the ADG of CID, Charu Sinha. He was produced before a magistrate for judicial remand.
The officer said that forged documents were allegedly used to facilitate cheating and financial irregularities within the cricketing body. Five other accused individuals had earlier been arrested in connection with the same case.
CID confirmed that further investigation is underway to establish the full extent of the financial misconduct and identify other potential beneficiaries of the alleged fraud.

title: Auto mutation of properties in Andhra Pradesh from August 1
summary: Auto mutation of properties in Andhra Pradesh from August 1. Developed jointly by the Municipal Administration & Urban Development Department and Registrations & Stamps Department, the system is set to be launched in 17 Municipal Corporations. The system integrates property registration with mutation, requiring no separate application by property owners. Aadhaar verification, PAN integration, geo-tagging, and electricity data syncing are among the digital features supporting the transformation.
content:
With the aim of streamlining urban governance, the Government of Andhra Pradesh has unveiled an instant auto-mutation system to automate property ownership updates during registration.
From August 1, the system will be rolled out in 17 Municipal Corporations to eliminate bureaucratic hurdles and bring speed, transparency, and efficiency to property transactions.
Developed jointly by the Municipal Administration & Urban Development Department and the Registrations & Stamps Department, the system integrates property registration with mutation, requiring no separate application by property owners.
Once the buyer clears applicable dues and mutation fee, ownership records are automatically updated in the municipal databases.
The initiative replaces the previously cumbersome manual process that involved multiple office visits, delays, and document duplication. The system supports residential and vacant land transactions, including part ownership transfers.
Principal Secretary S. Suresh Kumar on Friday called it a “citizen-first reform,” noting the system’s potential to enhance data accuracy, tax compliance, and urban planning. Aadhaar verification, PAN integration, geo-tagging, and electricity data syncing were among the digital features supporting the transformation.
Public awareness campaigns and staff training programmes were already underway, positioning Andhra Pradesh as a national leader in urban digital governance, he added.

title: Rich tributes paid to actor Kota Srinivasa Rao at condolence meeting in Vijayawada
summary: Rich tributes paid to actor Kota Srinivasa Rao at condolence meeting in Vijayawada
content:
The passing of Kota Srinivasa Rao, a towering figure in Indian cinema and public life, was marked with deep emotion and reverence at a condolence meeting held here on Friday. Andhra Pradesh BJP State president P.V.N. Madhav, speaking as the chief guest, described Kota Srinivasa Rao as a “fearless cultural warrior” who championed Hindutva ideals both on screen and in politics. He lauded Kota’s outspoken criticism of anti-Hindu rhetoric and his unwavering stand for Telugu pride in the film industry.
Minister for Health and Family Welfare Y. Satya Kumar Yadav highlighted Kota’s significant contributions to public service, especially his efforts to provide housing for the urban poor through the Valmiki Ambedkar Yojana (VAMBAY).
Veteran actor and former minister Babu Mohan, speaking over the phone, turned emotional as he reminisced about their decades-long friendship and memorable on-screen partnership.
Other dignitaries, including Kamineni Srinivasa Rao, Samineni Udayabhanu, Dara Sambayya, and several BJP and NDA leaders, paid heartfelt tributes to the late actor.
Kota Srinivasa Rao, who appeared in over 750 films and won nine Nandi Awards, was honoured with the Padma Shri for his unparalleled contributions to Indian cinema. His legacy of powerful performances and principled public service continues to inspire generations.
The event, led by NTR District BJP president Adduri Sriram, drew a large gathering of political leaders, film personalities, and admirers from across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

title: Kayaking takes centre stage at 11th edition of Malabar River Festival
summary: Two 15-year-olds shine at Malabar River Festival; thrilling competitions, international participants, and top-notch rescue team impress spectators.
content:
Two 15-year-olds from Madhya Pradesh stole the spotlight on the opening day of the 11th edition of the Malabar River Festival (MRF), which began at Pulikkayam, Kodenchery in Kozhikode on Friday (July 25). Garv Kokatery and Karishma Diwan braved the turbulent rapids of the Chalippuzha river to clinch first place in the Extreme Slalom competition in the men’s and women’s categories, respectively.
Akshay Asok from Kerala and Ayyappan Shyam from Karnataka secured second and third places in the men’s category, while Oxana Cherevchenko from Ukraine and Aayushi from Madhya Pradesh took second and third spots in the women’s category. However, disputes regarding the men’s category results have led to them being withheld for now.
A participant in the Intermediate Men’s Extreme Slalom event makes a splash as he leaps off the ramp at the Malabar River Festival, which began in Kodenchery, Kozhikode, on July 25.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                K. Ragesh
Ms. Cherevchenko, who arrived in India as a tourist, was an accidental kayaker. With just five days of training at Kodenchery, she participated in the event and went on to win the second prize. Giovanni Giorgi from Italy, who travelled to Kodenchery from his workplace in Bengaluru, also trained for five days and made it to the quarterfinals.
Students of Government UP School, Chembukadavu, on an excursion to witness the Malabar River Festival, which began at Pulikkayam, Kodenchery, in Kozhikode on July 25.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                K. Ragesh
The festival’s rescue team also won the hearts of the crowd on Friday. Due to the high water levels in the Chalippuzha, the preliminaries of the Extreme Slalom event were conducted as a Boater X event—a simpler format. However, the risk of kayaks capsizing or participants facing mishaps remained high.
In addition to the official rescue team led by Bishnu Guru from Nepal, scuba divers from the Fire and Rescue Services were present at the venue, ready for immediate response. Rescue personnel were stationed along the length of the river, from the starting point to the finish line—some in kayaks and others onshore with bamboo poles. Professional kayakers also assisted in ensuring safety. The riverbank was barricaded to prevent public access to the water, and scuba gear, dinghies, and ambulances were on standby.
Earlier in the day, Thiruvambady MLA Linto Joseph inaugurated the event, with Kodenchery grama panchayat president Alex Thomas Chembakasseri presiding over the function. Cultural programmes were held at Pulikkayam in the evening.
The professional segment of the Extreme Slalom competition, which will see participation from many international kayakers, is the highlight of the second day. The Downriver Race/Super Finals will be held at Pulloorampara on the Iruvazhinji river on Sunday (July 27), the final day of the festival.
The Malabar River Festival is organised by the Kerala Adventure Tourism Promotion Society and the Kozhikode District Tourism Promotion Council, with technical support from the Indian Kayaking and Canoeing Association.

title: Call for collective efforts to curb human trafficking
summary: Joint awareness programme by police and NGO on human trafficking prevention, laws, victim protection, and community involvement in combating trafficking.
content:
An awareness programme on “Prevention of Human Trafficking” was jointly organised by the Kumram Bheem Asifabad district police and Prajwala, an NGO, at the Agriculture Market Yard in the mandal headquarters town of Jainoor on Friday.
The programme was organised to raise public awareness on the critical issue, relevant laws, victim protection measures and the role of police and civil society in combating trafficking, a press release said.
Additional Superintendent of Police, Asifabad, S. Chitharanjan, and a host of other officials from various government departments, public representatives and others addressed the gathering.
Stating that human trafficking is a serious criminal offence, the speakers called upon people to come forward collectively to prevent such crimes and to immediately alert the police if they notice any suspicious activities around them.

title: 1950 Indiramma House beneficiaries found to be ineligible; benefit passed on to poor
summary: Telangana Housing Corporation ensures eligibility for Indiramma Houses, with 1,950 ineligible beneficiaries identified and rectified.
content:
Around 1,950 people were grantedIndiramma Housesagainst the rules. The benefit was passed on to eligible beneficiaries from poor backgrounds, said Telangana Housing Corporation’s managing director V.P. Gautham on Friday (July 25).
Altogether, 1.74 lakh beneficiaries began construction of houses. Of them, slabs were laid at 8,000 houses and the works are set to be completed at 5,000 houses.
Mr. Gautham said that objections were received against details of 12,700 beneficiaries. A comprehensive review on ground level was conducted by District Collectors, who submitted a report.
The 1,950 people who were later found to be ineligible either lived in a house with RCC slab, were government employees or earlier received a house under a scheme.

title: Drowning incidents on the rise in Thiruvananthapuram: district administration issues alert and safety guidelines
summary: 16 danger zones identified across the district
content:
With an alarming increase in drowning deaths across Thiruvananthapuram district, the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) in coordination with the district administration, has given shape to intensified preventive measures.
As part of such efforts, a year-long awareness campaign ‘Jeevanam’, aiming to highlight the importance of water safety and promote precautionary actions to prevent such tragedies.
According to Kerala Fire and Rescue Services statistics, a total of 352 people, including children and foreign nationals, have drowned in the district between 2019 and 2025. Among the victims, 315 were men and 37 women.
Under such circumstances, the district administration has initiated steps to officially declare certain water bodies as danger zones under the Disaster Management Act.
The 16 water bodies which have been designated as danger zones include bathing ghats at Kallar, Kollampuzha, Aruvipuram (Kallara), Mankayam, Chellanchy, Palode, Aruvikkara Dam, Ayiravalli Thampuran Temple ghat in Vattiyoorkavu; Neyyar reservoir; Moonnattumukku; Anandeshwaram; Poovanpara; Kundamankadavu; Koovakkudi bridge; Aruvipuram (Perumkadavila); and Pozhikkara.
As part of the action plan, the administration will install warning signboards, conduct awareness programmes and organise special initiatives in rural areas to educate people, including children, about water safety. Steps are also being taken to deploy trained lifeguards and set up first aid posts at identified danger zones.
The Kerala and Fire Rescue Services will conduct demonstrations and awareness classes at schools and for those working near water bodies to ensure wider outreach and impact.
The district administration has urged the public to remain cautious while near water bodies, especially in monsoon seasons, and to strictly adhere to safety instructions to avoid preventable tragedies.

title: TUDA allocates ₹5 crore for civic works in Srikalahasti
summary: The Tirupati Urban Development Authority (TUDA) has allocated ₹5 crore for the civic infrastructure works like roads, drains, footpaths, and greenery in the temple town of Srikalahasti.
content:
The Tirupati Urban Development Authority (TUDA) has allocated ₹5 crore for the civic infrastructure works like roads, drains, footpaths, and greenery in the temple town of Srikalahasti.
TUDA chairman Dollars C. Divakar Reddy on Friday conducted ‘A Day with TUDA chairman’, a first-of-its-kind interaction programme, with the line staff and other stakeholders in each of the nine constituencies falling under its purview. As the event started with Srikalahasti Constituency on Friday, he was joined by the local legislator Bojjala Venkata Sudhir Reddy.
Mr. Sudhir Reddy and Mr. Divakar Reddy, who embarked on a two-wheeler tour around the town, discussed the drain clogging issues with the sanitary workers and announced to renovate the storm water drains which are in a dilapidated condition in the old town.
The team inspected unauthorised buildings in Yelamandyam Panchayat and a layout at Inagalur. They held public meetings at Zilla Parishad High School in Munagalapalem and announced ₹15 lakh towards developing a playground.
The TUDA announced ₹1.6 crore for developing cement concrete roads for 2.5 km and sewerage channels at Tarakarama Nagar near Karakambadi.
TUDA Secretary N.V. Sreekanth Babu, Superintending Engineer Krishna Reddy, Chief Planning Officer Devi Kumari and horticulturist R. Malathi also took part.

title: Soldier killed in landmine blast in J&K’s Poonch
summary: Army soldier killed, two injured in landmine blast near LoC in Poonch, Jammu and Kashmir; condolences to family.
content:
An Army soldier was killed and two others were injured in a landmine blast near the Line of Control (LoC) in Poonch district ofJammu and Kashmiron Friday (July 25, 2025).
A spokesman of the Army’s White Knight Corps saidAgniveerLalit Kumar of 7 JAT Regiment made the supreme sacrifice while on an area domination patrol in general area of Krishna Ghati brigade following a mine blast. “We stand with the bereaved family in this hour of grief,” the Army said.
A Junior Commissioned Officer (JCO) was among the injured. The injured have been identified as Naib Subedar Hari Ram and Havaldar Gajendra Singh. Officials said the injured were immediately evacuated and airlifted to Army Base Hospital Udhampur for advanced treatment.
The incident took place around 12:15 p.m. near Victor Post of the Indian Army at village Salotri in Haveli tehsil when an M16 anti-personnel mine exploded during patrolling.

title: Karnataka HC notice to govt. on plea challenging project of developing Roerich estate as tourism hub
summary: High Court of Karnataka orders notice on PIL questioning development of Roerich Estate as tourism hub.
content:
The High Court of Karnataka on Friday ordered issue of notice to the Central and State governments on a PIL petition questioning the State government’s project of developing Roerich and Devika Rani Roerich Estate, Benglauru, as a tourism hub under the Central Government’s Special Assistance Scheme for development of iconic tourist centres.
A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice C.M. Joshi passed the order on the petition filed by R.R. Nagar I Care Trust, Bengaluru.
Questioning the approval for the project given by the State government in December 2024, the petitioner has contended that the development of the estate as a tourism hub is contrary to the provisions of the Roerich and Devika Rani Roerich Estate (Acquisition and Transfer) Act, 1996.
While seeking quashing of the approval granted for the project, the petitioner has sought a direction to the Roerich and Devika Rani Roerich Estate Board to conduct a scientific profiling of environmental, ecological, and wildlife factors of the estate, and to develop a plan towards object intent of the acquisition of the estate.
Also, a direction to the estate’s board has been sought to hold and declare the contiguous area of the estate as a biodiversity heritage site, or propose a conservation reserve for the remaining estate.

title: Govindachamy’s jailbreak points to larger conspiracy, says M.T. Ramesh
summary: BJP leader M.T. Ramesh alleges deep-rooted conspiracy in jailbreak, demands judicial inquiry and criticizes Election Commission and government decisions.
content:
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) State general secretary M.T. Ramesh has alleged that the  jailbreak by convict Govindachamy was not an isolated incident but the result of a deep-rooted conspiracy, claiming that such an escape would not have been possible without internal assistance.
Interacting with media in Thrissur on Friday, Mr. Ramesh stated that a person with  physical disability like Govindachamy could not have scaled prison walls on his own. “Locals were the ones who caught him. This highlights serious lapses on the part of the police and prison authorities,” he said.
He criticised the silence of the Jail Advisory Committee, which reportedly remained inactive until 11 a.m. following the incident. Mr. Ramesh further alleged that notorious criminals lodged in Kannur jail are being systematically aided with the tacit approval of the advisory committee. “The Home department must take responsibility, and the Chief Minister, who handles the Home portfolio, must respond to this grave failure,” he demanded.
The BJP leader also called for a judicial inquiry into the jailbreak to expose the truth behind the conspiracy.
Mr. Ramesh accused the Election Commission of manipulating the draft voter list to benefit the ruling Left Democratic Front (LDF) in the upcoming local body elections. “In many divisions, 60 to 70 votes have been transferred to unrelated wards. This is a blatant attempt to subvert the electoral process,” he said.
On the recent government decisions on school hours, Mr. Ramesh accused the LDF government of surrendering to religious organisations for political gain. “Instead of consulting experienced professionals in the education sector, the government sought opinions from organisations like Samastha. This is purely vote-bank politics,” he alleged.

title: Four days into the job, caretaker flees with gold and cash from Chandanagar apartment
summary: Caretaker steals gold and cash from Chandanagar flat, police on lookout for accused Mukkamalla Ravi, hired through Vashista Home Services.
content:
A caretaker who was employed just days earlier allegedly decamped with gold ornaments and cash from a flat in Sai Keerthi Estate, Friends Colony, Chandanagar, on Thursday evening.
According to the complaint, the accused, identified as Mukkamalla Ravi, 40, had been staying at the residence of Bussa Narsinga Rao and Chandrakala Bussa, the complainant’s in-laws, since July 20. He was hired through the Uppal branch of Vashista Home Services to assist the elderly couple.
On July 24, at around 5 p.m., Ravi told the family he was stepping out to get his shirt ironed. However, when he failed to return even after half an hour, the couple grew suspicious. Upon checking the puja room desk, they discovered that several gold ornaments and ₹40,000 in cash had gone missing.
Among the stolen jewellery were five tolas of stone bangles, three black bead chains weighing six tolas, a 3.5-tola bracelet, a chain with a locket weighing two tolas, a six-gram chain, an eight-gram stone chain, a red stone ring and a six-gram ring.
The family suspects the caretaker to be behind the theft. A case has been registered by the Chandanagar police, and efforts are on to trace the absconding accused.

title: DLSA Secretary inspects women’s hostel facilities in Guntur
summary: Guntur DLSA Secretary inspects women's campus facilities, encourages students to focus on studies, and directs improvements for better living conditions.
content:
Guntur District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) Secretary Syed Ziyauddin visited the Mahila Pranganam and the adjoining hostel within the women’s campus in Guntur. During the visit, he inspected the available facilities and interacted with students to assess the quality of services related to education, healthcare, food, and general welfare. He encouraged the students to concentrate on their studies and aspire to become responsible citizens.
While reviewing the infrastructure, Mr. Ziyauddin directed the hostel authorities to install a water purifier and a Reverse Osmosis (RO) plant to ensure access to safe drinking water. He also observed that two ceiling fans were not working and instructed staff to carry out immediate repairs.

title: Two-month campaign to strengthen MSMEs in E. Godavari begins
summary: RAMP programme in East Godavari district strengthens MSMEs with brand registration and skill improvement tools.
content:
A two-month campaign has been launched to strengthen the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) under the Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP) programme in East Godavari district.
The initiative is being led by the the District Industries Centre, with Joint Collector S. Chinna Ramudu as the Nodal Officer. The campaign aims to equip MSMEs with tools to register brands, logos and improve required skills to strengthen their units.

title: Man stabs estranged wife to death at a birthday party
summary: Man murders estranged wife at birthday party in Abdullapurmet, fleeing scene after stabbing her in front of guests.
content:
A birthday party in Abdullapurmet turned into a murder scene on Wednesday evening when a man stabbed his estranged wife to death in front of horrified guests, including children. The accused, identified as Srinu, fled the scene after the attack, said the police.
The victim, 35-year-old Satupati Sammakka, had come to attend her cousin’s daughter’s 14th birthday at a residence in SC Colony. At around 7 p.m., as the family was preparing to cut the cake, Srinu entered the house uninvited, said Abdullapurmet Inspector V. Ashok Reddy.
According to a complaint filed by the host, Satupati Rajeswari, Srinu quietly walked into the upper-floor room, sat in a corner and watched as the celebration began. As Sammakka stood nearby recording the moment on her phone, Srinu suddenly pulled out a knife and stabbed her three times in the neck.
The woman collapsed and bled to death on the spot. ‘’You had an affair with another man,‘’ Srinu was heard shouting before attempting to flee, as per the eyewitnesses. Panic gripped the room as adults screamed and children cried. Some guests tried to intervene, but Srinu brandished the knife at them, threatening to kill anyone who came close.
Despite the efforts of the landlord, Gunde Balraj, and neighbours Gunde Pavan and Gunde Shiva to catch him, Srinu escaped on a bike .
The complainant, Rajeswari, told police that Sammakka had left Srinu after frequent quarrels and domestic disputes, and had been staying separately in a rented house in the same locality for the past 15 days. Originally from Suryapet, she had moved to Abdullapurmet seeking some peace and distance.
Police have registered a case and said that efforts are underway to nab Srinu.

title: Film screenings as tribute to Shaji N. Karun in Thrissur
summary: Special screenings of Shaji N. Karun's films Piravi and Olu, with a memorial event "Shaji Ormakal" at Sree Theatre, Thrissur.
content:
In a tribute to filmmaker Shaji N. Karun, the Kerala State Chalachitra Academy in association with the IFFT Chalachitra Kendram in Thrissur will host special screenings of two of his landmark films on Saturday and Sunday at Sree Theatre, Thrissur.
The critically acclaimedPiraviwill be screened on Saturday at 9 a.m. On Sunday at 9 a.m.,Oluwill be showcased.
The inaugural session will include a memorial event titled “Shaji Ormakal” (Remembering Shaji), where personalities like Murali Cheeroth, chairperson, Kerala Lalithakala Akademi, film critics T. Krishnanunni, and I. Shanmukhadas will share their reflections on the filmmaker.

title: Taluk offices to be set up at Ponnampet, Kushalnagar soon: Karnataka Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda
summary: Karnataka Revenue Minister announces construction of new Taluk Administration Buildings in Kodagu district, emphasizing digital land record preservation.
content:
Karnataka Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda on Friday said that the construction of new Taluk Administration Buildings (Prajasaudha) in Ponnampet and Kushalnagar in Kodagu district will begin shortly.
He was speaking to media persons during his visit to the district. The Minister noted that though the two taluks were created more than 7 years ago, taluk offices have not yet been constructed, and said that the projects for the same would be expedited.
The government has sanctioned ₹8.65 crore each for the two buildings, and the tender process has been completed, he added.
Mr. Byre Gowda also inspected the proposed sites for the buildings and visited a bridge near Balyamandur. He said that the government was accelerating efforts to scan and digitally preserve original land ownership records across taluk offices to ensure landowners have guaranteed access to their documents.
“Preserving land records and making them accessible at the fingertips of landowners is the core objective of the Land Security Scheme,” said the Minister. The initiative aims to prevent loss, tampering, or forgery of land records, which often leads to disputes, he added.
With regard to digitisation of land records, the Minister said that the department has already scanned 33.5 crore pages of land records against the target of completing the scan of 100 crore pages of documents and records across Karnataka. This, he said, would serve as a legal guarantee for land records.
Mr. Byre Gowda emphasised the need for strict implementation of recent reforms in the Revenue Department and urged officials to adopt modern technology to deliver citizen services efficiently.
On the issue of recurring landslides in Kodagu, the Minister said that the government will allocate ₹50 crore for constructing retaining walls. The funds will be released soon by the Chief Minister, he added.
The Minister said full ownership rights would be extended to rightful landowners, and records dating back 30 to 40 years would be rectified where necessary, offering a long-term solution.
MLA for Virajpet A.S. Ponnanna apprised the Minister of rain damage in Kodagu district. Deputy Commissioner of Kodagu Venkat Raja, ZP CEO Anand Prakash Meena, and officials from PWD and various other departments were present.

title: Police step up drone surveillance in Anantapur
summary: Police in Anantapur have deployed drones to monitor deserted stretches and vulnerable spots to prevent crimes against women.
content:
Police in Anantapur have deployed drones to monitor deserted stretches and vulnerable spots to prevent crimes against women.
Speaking to the media on Friday, Superintendent of Police P. Jagadeesh said that the initiative aims to stop incidents of eve‑teasing, harassment, and other offences.
The Bukkarayasamudram police led special Shakti Teams in carrying out aerial surveillance over sensitive locations. Drones were flown over isolated farmlands, open grounds, parks, and other vulnerable spots on the city outskirts.
“With drone monitoring, we can cover wide areas in real time and alert ground teams instantly,” SP Jagadeesh said. Our priority is to ensure that women feel safe while travelling or passing through these regions. Anyone caught harassing or attempting to harm women will face strict action, he added.
The SP said that the police teams have identified some vulnerable hotspots known for anti-social activities, and the drone surveillance would be stepped up at these targeted places.
He said that the move mustered overwhelming support from the villagers, particularly women. “These initiatives have started enhancing the trust of the public in the police and made women feel secure,” he added.

title: Tight security in Tiruchi, Ariyalur for PM’s visit
summary: Security has been stepped up at the Tiruchi International Airport and in and around a hotel in the city in view of the visit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday
content:
Security has been stepped up at the Tiruchi International Airport and in and around a hotel in the city in view of the visit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday.
Mr. Modi is scheduled to  participate in the Aadi Thiruvathirai festival at Gangaikonda Cholapuram in Ariyalur district on Sunday and release a coin in honour of the King Rajendra Chola I.
The police said Mr. Modi will land in Tiruchi on a special flight from Thoothukudi at around 10.30 p.m. on Saturday and stay in a hotel situated on the Collector Office Road.
Mr. Modi will proceed to the airport on Sunday morning by road and board a chopper to Gangaikonda Cholapuram to participate in the function which is to be organised near the temple.  Mr. Modi will return by chopper to the Tiruchi airport and leave for New Delhi in the afternoon,  the sources said.
A multi-layer security has been put in place at the airport where anti-sabotage teams have been deployed. About 1,500 police personnel have been mobilised by the Tiruchi City Police in connection with the Prime Minister’s visit.
Security has been heightened at Gangaikonda Cholapuram with teams of police personnel deployed at the helipad, venue, and in the surrounding areas.  Around 2,200 police personnel are being deployed at Gangaikonda Cholapuram, the sources added.

title: Crime prevention is top priority, says Kurnool SP
summary: The Kurnool police have stepped up measures for protection of women and children by focusing on renewed cybercrime awareness initiatives.
content:
The Kurnool police have stepped up measures for protection of women and children by focusing on renewed cybercrime awareness initiatives.
Speaking at an awareness campaign at Pullareddy Engineering College auditorium here on Friday, Superintendent of Police Vikrant Patil said that crime prevention was the top priority of the police department. “We have launched many strengthened measures for the protection of women and children to sensitise them against crimes, particularly in the digital age with an alarming rise in the misuse of technology,” he said.
The SP informed the students about the State government’s initiatives, such as the Shakti App, Shakti WhatsApp services, and dedicated Shakti Teams, urging them to save key emergency numbers — Shakti WhatsApp 7993485111, Kurnool Shakti WhatsApp 7777877700, Dial 100, Dial 112, Child Helpline 1098, and Cybercrime 1930.
All the police stations across the district were instructed to arrange at least one awareness programme daily in schools and colleges. “The students were told to report eve-teasing or harassment immediately,” the SP said.
Deputy SP (Mahila Police wing) J. Babu Prasad said that even educated women are falling victim to online fraud. The students were advised to use social media platforms only for educational and career purposes.

title: Strong wind, heavy rain wreak widespread damage in Kottayam
summary: Heavy rain and strong winds cause widespread damage in Kottayam and Pathanamthitta districts, leading to power outages and traffic disruptions.
content:
Heavy rain and strong winds wreaked widespread damage across Kottayam district on Friday (July 25, 2025). According to reports, several houses were damaged and agricultural crops suffered extensive destruction in various areas.
The most severe damage occurred in the Pampady, Kooroppada, Akalakunnam and Meenadom panchayats. Traffic disruptions were reported after a tree fell on the road in Kooroppada, while downed electricity poles and wires created panic among residents. Consequently, electricity supply was interrupted in the Kooroppada and Madapad regions.
A branch of a teak tree fell onto the parish hall of Meenadom Valiya Church (St. Thomas Orthodox Church), damaging the roofing sheets. An event is scheduled to take place here on Saturday.
Traffic came to a halt along the Kottayam-Kumarakom Road after a large tree was uprooted due to strong winds. The fallen tree obstructed the road near the Kumarakom Chula Puthan area, leading to further disruptions in electricity supply. The main electric line in the Aymanam section was damaged, resulting in power outages. A major disaster was averted as no vehicles were passing at the time of the incident.
In another occurrence, a tree on CMS College Road succumbed to the heavy winds and rain in the afternoon. The tree, located within the college campus, fell onto the power lines and the road but was fortunately wedged between two compound walls, preventing a more serious incident. The College was closed as the District Collector had declared a holiday for educational institutions in Kottayam taluk. Therefore, there were no students or vehicles on the college road, further averting another disaster.
Water levels in all major rivers in Kottayam, such as the Meenachil, Manimala, and Muvattupuzha rivers, continued to surge throughout the day. The Meenachil, which flowed in full spate, stood close to the danger level in the downstream areas.
In view of he continuing rain, Kottayam District Collector has declared a holiday for all educational institutions on Saturday (July 26) as well
In Pathanamthitta, squally winds caused widespread damage, particularly in Ranni, where several electric poles were uprooted. At Marthoma Junction, numerous shops and commercial establishments sustained damages due to falling trees. Power distribution was disrupted across most parts of the district.

title: Over 6,000 people from Chennai and its peripheral areas receive pattas
summary: State government distributes over 6,000 land pattas in Chennai, addressing challenges with over 1.33 lakh pattas issued so far.
content:
Over 6,000 beneficiaries from Chennai and its peripheral areas receivedpattasat an event organised by the State government on Friday.
Ministers K.K.S.S.R. Ramachandran, S. Muthusamy, and P.K. Sekarbabu distributed thepattasto the beneficiaries at the function held at the Sir Ramaswami Mudaliar Higher Secondary School in Ambattur.
As there were some challenges in issuing thepattasin Chennai and its peripheral areas, the State government had constituted a committee to look into them. Based on its recommendations, over 1.33 lakhpattashave been issued in Chennai so far, an official release said.
Chennai Mayor R. Priya, Sriperumbudur MP T.R. Baalu, legislators Joseph Samuel, Thayagam Kavi, K. Ganapathy, and A. Vetriazhagan were among those present.

title: R. Gopalakrishnan is SCR new DRM
summary: R. Gopalakrishnan is SCR new DRM
content:
A 1998 batch Indian Railway Traffic Service (IRTS) officer, R. Gopalakrishnan, has assumed charge as the Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) of Secunderabad Division, SCR., on Thursday. Prior to the posting he was holding Additional Divisional Railway Manager, Secunderabad Division.
A mechanical engineer from IIT Delhi, an MBA from the Faculty of Management Studies (FMS), University of Delhi, and Ph.D. in Engineering Systems and Design from the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), Mr. Gopalakrishnan has managed operations and commercial functions in the highly complex Mumbai suburban railway system and led nationwide petroleum logistics at the Railway Board.
A major milestone in his career was the establishment of the Data Analytics Unit of Indian Railways which developed the Artificial Intelligence and Data Strategy and worked on seat capacity optimisation in reserved trains, automated freight terminal allotment and was part of the national-level committee to evaluate railway junction capacity, said a press release.

title: India aware of China's aim to become 'maritime power', closely monitors developments in IOR: Centre
summary: India monitors China's maritime presence in the Indian Ocean Region closely to safeguard its security and economic interests.
content:
India is aware of China’s stated objective of becoming a maritime power, and New Delhi closely monitors all developments in the Indian Ocean Region impinging on its security and economic interests and takes appropriate measures to safeguard them, the Centre informed Parliament on Friday (July 25, 2025).
In a written response to a query in the Lok Sabha, Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh also said, “Our relations with countries in the Indian Ocean Region are comprehensive and long-standing, based on their own merit and are independent of their relations with any third countries.”
The Ministry of External Affairs was asked whether China’s growing presence in the Indian Ocean Region is a strategic challenge for India.
“The government is aware of China’s stated objective of becoming a maritime power. As part of this strategy, China is developing ports and other infrastructure facilities in the littoral countries in the Indian Ocean Region,” he said.
China also has a naval and maritime presence in the Indian Ocean Region, including through anti-piracy escort missions, port calls and deployment of research and survey vessels, the MoS said.
Government closely monitors all developments in the Indian Ocean Region impinging on India’s security and economic interests and takes appropriate measures to safeguard India’s interests, he added.
Countries such as Sri Lanka, the Maldives and Mauritius occupy a central place in India’s ‘Neighbourhood First’ Policy and MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) vision, the MoS said.
“Our political relations with countries of the region are strong, trade and investment ties are being augmented, development projects and infrastructural cooperation are progressing, and there is broad-based engagement across all sectors,” he added.

title: Home Minister reviews cyclone preparedness; directs officials to stay alert
summary: Home Minister directs officials to prepare for cyclone, urges public to take precautions, and provides emergency contact numbers.
content:
Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha has directed officials of various departments to remain vigilant in view of the approaching cyclone and take all necessary measures to prevent loss of life.
On Friday, Ms. Anitha visited the State Emergency Operation Centre at the office of the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) and reviewed the cyclone’s trajectory, rainfall trends, and flood situation in various districts. The review was conducted alongside APSDMA Managing Director Prakhar Jain, Executive Director Ch. Venkata Deepak, and other senior officials.
Speaking on the occasion, the Home Minister said the cyclone is expected to move towards Odisha, West Bengal, and Jharkhand within the next 24 hours. Coastal Andhra Pradesh is likely to receive heavy rainfall, while moderate showers are predicted across the rest of the State. She urged fishermen to refrain from venturing into the sea for the next 72 hours and advised the public to avoid staying under trees, electric poles, and in old or damaged buildings. For emergencies, citizens can reach out through Control Room numbers 112, 1070, or 1800 425 0101.
Meanwhile, officials of the Sri Durga Malleswara Swamyvarla Devasthanam closed the ghat road to Indrakeeladri on Friday due to continuous rainfall over the past two days. Police and Endowments Department staff have set up pickets and are restricting vehicle movement on the road as a precautionary measure.

title: Karnataka Revenue Minister directs implementation of e-office systems in all districts
summary: Karnataka Revenue Minister directs complete implementation of e-office systems for efficient and transparent file clearance online.
content:
Karnataka Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda on Friday said that the Deputy Commissioners and Tahsildars in all districts have been directed to completely implement e-office systems for clearing files online.
The adoption of e-office software has to be made completely in order to ensure a fully paperless office for improving efficiency and transparency, and all files concerned with the department have to be cleared digitally, the Minister added.
Speaking to reporters in Madikeri, the Minister said that e-office adoption will ensure safety of files and records, and therefore cannot be lost. The disposal of files cannot be delayed citing reasons like postal delay and so on; the records cannot be concealed, he added. He said that e-office adoption has to reach till the level of village accountants.
So far, 4,000 Village Accountants (VA) have been given laptops to facilitate online services, and the remaining ones would also be getting laptops soon so that the services get faster, the Minister said.
Mr. Byre Gowda said that steps have been taken to provide office space to VAs in gram panchayat offices so that the public get to meet them. All these years, the VAs had no offices and steps for providing them with office spaces had been taken based on the public feedback, the Minister added.
Out of 8,500 VAs in the State, nearly 2,000 VAs have got offices and 5,000 others will get offices soon. In Kodagu, 108 VAs have received office space in 102 gram panchayat offices.
Mr. Byre Gowda said ₹1 lakh crore has been credited into the accounts of 4.5 crore people in the form of the guarantee schemes. “This has become possible due to technology adoption. The benefits have been extended without the beneficiaries coming to the offices. This implementation has set an example for others. The initiative has now become a model,” he said.
Kodagu Deputy Commissioner will prioritise works in areas identified as ‘landslide prone’ for the safety of people, the Minister told reporters. Steps are being taken based on the list of places identified susceptible to landslides, he said.
MLAs A.S. Ponnanna and Mantar Gowda, Deputy Commissioner Venkataraja, and others were present.

title: Three two-wheeler riders killed in road accident near Mayanur
summary: Three persons, including two women, were killed in a road accident near Mayanur in Karur district on Friday evening when the two-wheeler they were riding was hit by a car on the Tiruchi–Karur National Highway
content:
Three persons, including two women, were killed in a road accident near Mayanur in Karur district on Friday evening when the two-wheeler they were riding was hit by a car on the Tiruchi–Karur National Highway.
The deceased were identified as N. Suresh Kumar alias Dhanapal, 38, a mason from Mayanur, who was riding the two-wheeler. The pillion riders were P. Chitra, 30, a construction worker from Lalapettai, and I. Ramayee, 58, from Mayanur.
The accident occurred when the three were returning home from work. A car travelling from Tiruchi towards Karur reportedly went out of control and rammed the two-wheeler. All the three died on the spot.
The occupants of the car reportedly fled the scene after the accident.
Mayanur police arrived at the location and sent the bodies to the Karur Government Medical College and Hospital for post-mortem. A case has been registered and investigation is under way.

title: Congress finalises heads of 22 govt.-owned boards, corporations
summary: Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and Deputy D.K. Shivakumar finalize names for government board chairpersons, pending public announcement.
content:
Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and his deputy D.K. Shivakumar have reportedly finalised the names of 22 legislators and party leaders for the posts of chairperson of the government-owned boards and corporations.
The names were finalised after a meeting with AICC general secretary in charge of Karnataka Randeep Singh Surjewala in Delhi on Thursday night. The list will be made public after a couple of days, party sources said.
Meanwhile, sources said both party MLAs and leaders had been given equal preference in the appointments. After Mr. Surjewala’s meetings with Ministers and MLAs in Bengaluru, sources said the names suggested by Ministers/legislators had been given priority in the appointments.
Till now, the government has appointed 42 legislators as chairpersons of various boards and corporations.
However, directors and members of boards/corporations have not yet been appointed.
Following the AICC general secretary’s meeting with legislators, the government released ₹50 crore to each MLA for undertaking development works in their respective constituencies.
Sources said candidates for the four vacant seats in the Karnataka Legislative Council had also not been finalised. The names would be finalised after senior leader Rahul Gandhi vets the list in August.
Earlier in Delhi, Mr. Siddaramaiah participated in the ‘Bhagidari Nyay Sammelan’ of the other backward classes. Party leaders, including AICC chief Mallikarjun Kharge, Mr. Gandhi, K.C. Venugopal, and Anil Jaihind, participated in it.

title: Govindachamy’s escape exposes cracks in high-security prisons in Kerala
summary: Jailbreak by Govindachamy exposes security flaws in Kerala prisons, prompting urgent review and discussions on system challenges.
content:
The jailbreak by rape and murder convict Govindaswamy, alias Govindachamy, from the Kannur Central Prison has brought renewed attention to the glaring security inadequacies at certain high-security prisons in Kerala.
The incident spotlit long-standing infrastructure inadequacies, most notably the absence of electric fencing at the prison, despite earlier proposals to bolster perimeter security.
Official sources confirmed that security audits had been undertaken across the State’s correctional facilities and would now be intensified in the wake of the escape. It would entail a review of the surveillance and lighting systems in the State’s prisons.
Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan will convene a high-level meeting on Saturday to discuss precautionary measures to prevent further lapses. The State Police Chief, Director General of Prisons and Correctional Services, and the Secretary of the Home department will participate in the meeting.
The Deputy Inspector General of Prisons (North Zone) has been tasked with leading an internal inquiry that will examine lapses that may have facilitated Govindachamy’s escape. The jail authorities reportedly came to know about the escape only during the regular morning roll call.
An official privy to the matter stated that the police would also investigate whether wardens conducted surprise checks of cells without adhering to a predictable timetable. The probe would also likely examine whether night wardens undertook regular rounds inside the prison and patrolled the vast area outside the walls at night, the official said.
He stated that prima facie information suggested that Govindachamy had stocked civilian clothes and bedsheets to improvise a ‘rope’ in the high-security cell, indicating an alleged lapse on the part of the prison administration. “There seemed to have been no rigorous bed checks in Govindachamy’s cell, despite the authorities categorising him as a high-risk prisoner. Prison rules insist that wardens file a checklist after cell inspections,” he added.
The Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services are preparing to approach the State government to fast-track the installation of advanced perimeter security, including long-pending electric fencing projects.
The government had several years ago proposed to erect electric fencing and install laser-scanning systems at all jails in the State. However, while some Central Prisons, such as Poojappura, are equipped with electric fencing, the Kannur Central Prison remains vulnerable, with earlier proposals for upgrades yet to be implemented. Delays, officials said, had been exacerbated by a persistent fund crunch and bottlenecks on the part of implementing agencies.
The jailbreak will also reignite discussions on the wider challenges facing Kerala’s prison system, including overcrowding and staff shortages.
Official statistics indicate that the State’s 57 prisons have long surpassed their authorised capacities. These correctional facilities currently accommodate 10,662 inmates, far higher than their combined limit of 7,828. They include 4,224 convicts and 1339 undertrials.

title: Kerala mulling credits, semester system for higher secondary classes
summary: Multiple proposals being mulled as the State enters last phase of its comprehensive curriculum revision
content:
Introduction of credits and a semester system for higher secondary classes is one of the proposals being mulled as the State enters the last phase of its comprehensive curriculum revision for school education.
A conclave held in the State capital on Friday to hold discussions with stakeholders and garner public opinion on the higher secondary curriculum revision that is set to begin soon underlined the need to consider the recent changes in the higher education sector, particularly the implementation of the four-year undergraduate programme (FYUGP) in the State, when deciding on the direction of the higher secondary curriculum reforms.
Even though the credit system has not been fully realised nationally, the State is pondering if students can earn credits not only through project and assignments but also National Cadet Corps and National Service Scheme activities.
Reducing the academic burden on students is also under consideration. Making language subjects optional is one way being explored. Higher secondary students can study Indian or foreign languages online and earn credits.
This will also allow students to focus more on core subjects. For instance, Humanities students currently unable to pursue Economics and Mathematics together can do so if they choose to study one language through SCOLE-Kerala.
Decisions though will have to be taken on aspects such as the number of credits that students can earn and if schools have the wherewithal to implement such proposals – such as faculty and infrastructure.
Presenting the concept note for the higher secondary curriculum revision, State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT) director Jayaprakash R.K. pointed out that curriculum revision at the national level was guided by the National Education Policy under which the National Credit Framework provided for 1,200 hours of learning and 160 credits for classes XI and XII. The FYUGP provided more choice to students in pursuing courses and gave importance to skill education. “When thinking about higher secondary curriculum reforms, the transformations in higher education in the State have to be taken into account.”
He also pointed out that importance of skill courses and competency development. The reforms also raised the question of how the 21st century skills could be passed on to students in the classroom, especially at a time when technology was making huge leaps and artificial intelligence had found its way into classrooms, he said.
Dr. Jayaprakash explained the schedule for the revision process. Public discussions would be held at the district-levels from August 1 to 15. Workshops on conceptualising ideas, textbook writing, and editing will follow. Expert committee meetings will be held in December. Scrutiny and curriculum subcommittee meetings will follow. The curriculum steering committee will meet in February and the textbooks will be ready for printing by March 10.
Minister for Finance K.N. Balagopal who inaugurated the conclave said the achievements in the public education sector could be carried forward only through constant improvements. Minister for General Education V. Sivankutty presided.

title: ‘Declare Rajendra Chola’s birthday as world water management day’
summary: Bharatiya Kisan Sangh State secretary N. Veerasekaran has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to declare the day of Aadi Thiruvathirai, the birth star of Rajendra Chola I, as World Water Management Day in memory of the Chola emperor
content:
Bharatiya Kisan Sangh State secretary N. Veerasekaran has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to declare the day of Aadi Thiruvathirai, the birth star of Rajendra Chola I, as World Water Management Day in memory of the Chola emperor.
In a representation addressed to the Prime Minister, Mr. Veerasekaran highlighted the water management legacy of the Chola dynasty, particularly Rajendra Chola’s contributions. Interconnected tanks, lakes, and sluices created under the dynasty formed a sustainable water grid, which continues to support agriculture in the Cauvery delta.  Mr. Veerasekaran also urged the Centre  to instituted awards for farmers, panchayat leaders, engineers, and institutions contributing to water conservation.

title: Tripura Governor hails medical advancement
summary: Tripura Governor N. Indrasena Reddy has hailed the medical fraternity for embracing modern technology to get medical advancement to the reach of common man.
content:
Tripura Governor N. Indrasena Reddy has hailed the medical fraternity for embracing modern technology to get medical advancement to the reach of common man.
Speaking at a golden jubilee international conference organised by Sri Venkateswara Medical College Alumni Association (SVMCAA) here on Friday, the Governor recalled that it was during the Covid-19 pandemic that the technology had come to the fore.
“As technology advances, we need to keep abreast of the same and the syllabus we studied decades back has to be thoroughly revised to meet the current day needs,” he said.
Tirupati District Collector S. Venkateswar saw a greater need for the alumni networks not only in promoting their alma mater, but also in conducting conferences to let the information on medical advancement percolate to all levels.
MLC Cipai Subramanyam, TTD board member G. Bhanuprakash Reddy, SVMCAA Chairperson Rayapu Ramesh Babu, SVMC Principal G. Ravi Prabhu, Ruia Hospital Superintendent R. Radha and Government Maternity Hospital Superintendent K. Parthasarathy took part.

title: Two siblings murdered at Avudaiyarkoil in dispute over sale of a used two-wheeler
summary: In a case of double murder, two brothers were hacked to death by an armed gang at Avudaiyarkoil in the district on Thursday night triggering tension in the locality. The police gave the names of the dead as K. Kannan, 35, and K. Karthi, 29
content:
In a case of double murder, two brothers were hacked to death by an armed gang at Avudaiyarkoil in the district on Thursday night triggering tension in the locality. The police gave the names of the dead as K. Kannan, 35, and K. Karthi, 29.
The siblings were murdered a few metres away from their house by the gang. The killers escaped on a couple of two-wheelers, the police said.
A quarrel over sale of a used two-wheeler is said to be the reason for the murderous attack. Kannan’s relative recently sold a two-wheeler to a person and a quarrel ensued over payment a few days ago.  Kannan spoke in support of his relative while Muthukumar was on the side of the buyer. This apparently led to a scuffle between Kannan and Muthukumar eventually leading to the double murder.  The body of the victims were sent to the Pudukottai Government Medical College Hospital for autopsy.
The family members of the victims blocked the Avudaiyarkoil-Aranthangi road for sometime on Friday morning in protest against the double murder and demanded compensation.  Special teams constituted to nab the killers detained seven persons, including Muthukumar and Kalidas, in connection with the case.  The Avudaiyarkoil police registered a case.
The bodies of the victims were handed over to the family members later in the day.
A compensation of ₹12 lakh was given to the victims’ family, said police sources.

title: Bhoomi puja performed for new grievance cell, media gallery at Guntur SP Office
summary: Bhoomi puja held for new Grievance Cell and Media Gallery at Guntur SP office sponsored by VIT-AP University.
content:
A bhoomi puja was conducted on Friday for the construction of a new Grievance Cell and Media Gallery at the office of the Superintendent of Police (SP) in Guntur district. The project is being sponsored by VIT-AP University as part of its corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative.
Superintendent of Police, Guntur district, S. Satish Kumar, along with VIT-AP University Vice-Chancellor S.V. Kota Reddy and Registrar Jagadish Chandra, took part in the ceremony.
The SP expressed his gratitude to the VIT-AP University management for their support, stating that the new facilities would enable police personnel to better serve visitors with grievances and interact with the media in a more organised manner. Mr. Kota Reddy noted that the project reflects the university’s commitment to community partnership. He also acknowledged the support and encouragement of Chancellor G. Viswanathan and Vice-President G.V. Selvam in taking up the initiative.

title: Committee to examine parameters for fee regulation
summary: Committee to examine parameters for fee regulation
content:
The Telangana Admissions and Fee Regulatory Committee (TAFRC) on Friday vide an order appointed a Committee of Officers to examine the parameters for fee fixation and suggest revised parameters.
The exercise pertains to private unaided professional colleges and must be completed while adhering to orders of the Supreme Court and the High Court.
The committee shall explore and identify relevant indicators and benchmarks to be considered for determining fee structures, and other factors impacting the cost of education, the order said.
As per TAFRC, the committee will be headed by Council of Higher Education Chairman V. Balakista Reddy, and members include: Commissioner of Technical Education A. Sridevasena, Director, Scheduled Caste Development Department, N. Kshitija, Director, State Audit Department, M. Venkateshwar Rao, Director, Town and Country Planning S. Devender Reddy, Secretary TGCHE, Sriram Venkatesh, Registrar, JNTUH, K. Venkateswara Rao, Dean (Engineering) Osmania University A. Krishnaiah, and any other two subject experts as per the chairperson.

title: Incriminating documents, ₹72 lakh cash seized in ED searches linked to HMDA scam
summary: ED Hyderabad searches locations, recovers cash and documents in assets case involving suspended official and real estate firms.
content:
The Directorate of Enforcement (ED), Hyderabad Zonal Office, carried out search operations on Thursday, July 24 at three locations in the city in connection with a disproportionate assets case involving Siva Balakrishna, the suspended Director of HMDA and Secretary-in-charge of Telangana Real Estate Regulatory Authority (TSRERA), and others.
These searches led to the recovery of several incriminating documents and unaccounted cash amounting to ₹72 lakh.
Searches were conducted at the residences of directors and partners of three real estate firms, Sree Krishna Constructions, Quorizon Spaces and Udaya SSV Projects.
The searches were conducted under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002. The ED’s investigation stems from an FIR registered by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), Hyderabad, which accused Siva Balakrishna and others of accumulating wealth far exceeding their known sources of income. The FIR alleged that properties were acquired not only in his name but also in the names of family members and benamis.
According to the ED, Balakrishna received illicit payments from builders in exchange for favourable actions such as building plan sanctions and land use changes. These proceeds of crime were used to acquire both movable and immovable assets across various fronts. The agency said earlier searches conducted on July 2 at the premises of Balakrishna and his brother resulted in the seizure of incriminating documents and property records.
The documents suggested extensive dealings with multiple realtors. Investigators also found that Balakrishna had parked funds with certain builders and was using vehicles registered under their names. Another FIR by the ACB alleged that Balakrishna received illegal gratification for facilitating clearance of a high-rise project by M/s Udaya SSV Projects at Narsingi. Further investigation is ongoing.

title: Collector reviews monsoon preparedness in Thrissur
summary: District Disaster Management Authority reviews monsoon preparedness in Thrissur, emphasizing road maintenance, waterlogging solutions, relief camp establishment, and safety measures.
content:
A meeting of the District Disaster Management Authority convened by District Collector Arjun Pandiyan on Friday reviewed monsoon preparedness by various departments across Thrissur district.
The Collector gave instructions  to ensure continuous maintenance and repairs of potholes on roads to guarantee commuter safety. He also stressed the need for compliance with directions issued in previous meetings on road safety, and urged officials to verify that these are being implemented effectively.
To address waterlogging issues in the Cherpu-Pullu region, the Subcollector has been assigned to coordinate efforts. Officials reported that removal of weeds and vegetation has already begun. Orders have been issued to open closed sluices and bunds. The meeting proposed forming squads to implement these instructions promptly.
Considering the need for a permanent relief camp in the area, the Collector directed the Thrissur tahsildar to identify land and send a proposal to the government. He also instructed the Public Works department Buildings Division to prepare a cost estimate for  this.
The Collector stressed that all school buildings must be inspected by either the Local Self Government department’s (LSGD) Public Works engineer or a certified structural engineer, and only those certified fit for use should be operational. Buildings lacking fitness certification must not be used for classes.
He also instructed that precautionary measures be taken in landslip-prone areas.
The Kerala State Electricity Board was directed to inspect and replace or secure damaged or leaning electric posts and wires, particularly around schools and public spaces. To speed up the damage assessment caused by the monsoon so far, the Collector issued directions to tahsildars and the LSGD executive engineers.

title: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy hailed as ‘beacon of hope’
summary: Speakers at the “Dr. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy Memorial Awards-2025” hailed him as a beacon of hope for the current and future generations in terms of honesty, integrity and public service.
content:
Speakers at the “Dr. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy Memorial Awards-2025” hailed him as a beacon of hope for the current and future generations in terms of honesty, integrity and public service.
The event was organised by Association of Grassroots Studies and Research of India (AGRASRI) in association with Sri Venkateswara University’s Department of Political Science and Public Administration on Friday.
APPSC former chairman Y. Venkatrami Reddy and Andhra Pradesh State Administrative Tribunal former chairman Justice G. Yethirajulu hailed the first Chief Minister of combined Andhra Pradesh for prioritising rural development and agricultural advancement by improving irrigation, providing subsidies for farmers and promoting modern technologies.
SVU Vice-Chancellor Ch. Appa Rao recalled Neelam’s vision behind founding the varsity in the backward Rayalaseema region. “Dr. Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy Vishishta Ratna” award was presented to Prof. Venkatrami Reddy, ‘Nyaya Shiromani’ to former Judge of Andhra Pradesh High Court Justice B. Sesha Sayana Reddy, ‘Vidya Shiromani’ to former Vice Chancellor of GITAM University Prof. S. Dayananda and ‘Vaidya Shiromani’ to noted Ayurvedic doctor Dr. G.V. Purrnachand.
A special souvenir published in the honour of the awardees was released on the occasion. SVU political Science head B.V. Muralidhar, AGRASRI Director D. Sundar Ram and All India Radio retired Director A. Malleswara Rao also spoke at the event.

title: Rajendranagar Deputy Commissioner in ACB net
summary: Deputy Commissioner of GHMC arrested for accepting ₹2 lakh bribe from hotel owner in Rajendranagar, under investigation by ACB.
content:
A Deputy Commissioner of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC), posted in Rajendranagar was arrested by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Friday, July 25 for allegedly accepting a bribe of ₹2 lakh from a hotel owner.
According to the ACB, the accused officer, K. Ravi Kumar, who is currently serving as Deputy Commissioner of Circle-11 in Rajendranagar municipality, demanded ₹5 lakh from the complainant in exchange for not taking action against the hotel for not being up to code. The bribe was demanded for overlooking irregularities found in the hotel kitchen during an inspection and to prevent reputational damage or possible seizure of the establishment.
The ACB said the officer received ₹2 lakh from the complainant, which was recovered from him during the operation. Following his arrest, he was sent to judicial remand. The case is currently under investigation.
Authorities have urged the public to report any instances of bribery or corruption by public servants by calling the ACB’s toll-free number 1064. Complaints can also be made via WhatsApp, Facebook, or X through ACB Telangana’s official channels. The identity of complainants will be kept confidential.

title: West Bengal Governor returns Aparajita Bill to State govt. for reconsideration
summary: West Bengal Governor returns Aparajita Bill over death penalty concerns, raising questions over harsh punishment provisions.
content:
Raising concerns over the death penalty provisions inThe Aparajita Women and Child (West Bengal Criminal Laws Amendment) Bill, 2024,West Bengal Governor C.V. Ananda Bose has returned the legislation to the State government for further consideration.
“One of the proposed amendments seeks to enhance the punishment for rape under Section 64 of the BNS, 2023, raising it from the existing minimum of 10 years to life imprisonment for the remainder of one’s life or death. The Ministry of Home Affairs has termed this change as excessively harsh and disproportionate,” an official of Raj Bhawan, Kolkata, said.
ALSO WATCHWatch: What does Bengal’s ‘Aparajita’ Anti-Rape Bill entail?
The West Bengal Legislative Assembly had unanimously passed the Aparajita Bill on September 3, 2024, introducing stringent punishment in cases involving sexual assault. The Bill was sent to President Droupadi Murmu by the Governor on September 6, 2024.
The legislation, which was passed 25 days after the rape and murder of a doctor at R.G. Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata, provides for the death penalty in five categories of offences — rape, rape by a police officer or public servant, rape causing death or resulting in a persistent vegetative state, gang rape, and repeat offenders.
Raj Bhawan officials pointed out that the Bill proposes to make the death penalty mandatory in cases where the victim dies or is left in a vegetative state under Section 66 of the BNS. “The Ministry of Home Affairs has raised concerns over the removal of judicial discretion in such cases,” the official said.
According to Raj Bhawan, the Bill also proposes to delete Section 65 of the BNS, 2023, thereby eliminating the distinction in punishment for the rape of women under 16 and under 12 years of age. “The Ministry has observed that the removal of such classification violates the principle of proportionality in sentencing,” the official added.
The development comes amid repeated appeals by the Trinamool Congress government urging the Union government to grant assent to the Bill. A delegation of Trinamool Congress MPs met President Droupadi Murmu on February 13, to press for early approval of the legislation.
Certain legal experts had described the Aparajita Bill as a knee-jerk response by the West Bengal government.

title: Ranjith Sreenivas murder case: death penalty for 10th accused
summary: Mavelikara court sentences Navas to death for BJP leader's murder; part of PFI-SDPI group retaliating RSS killing.
content:
The Mavelikara Additional District Sessions Court-I on Friday awarded the death penalty to the 10th accused in the murder of BJP leader Ranjith Sreenivas.
The convict, Navas, 52, is a native of Palace Ward in Alappuzha municipality. Earlier, on January 30, 2024, the court had awarded the death penalty to 14 of the 15 convicts in the case. Though the court had found Navas guilty of the charges against him, it had not pronounced his sentence at the time as he was undergoing medical treatment at a hospital.
On Friday, Judge V.G. Sreedevi sentenced Navas, who was produced via video conferencing, to be hanged by the neck till death.
Sreenivas, a lawyer and the State secretary of the BJP’s front for Other Backward Classes (OBCs), was brutally hacked to death at his house at Vellakinar in Alappuzha municipality on the morning of December 19, 2021. He was murdered in front of his mother, wife, and daughter.
All the 15 convicts, hailing from various parts of Alappuzha, belonged to the now proscribed Popular Front of India (PFI) and its political arm, the Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI).
According to investigators, Sreenivas’ killing was a retaliatory strike to avenge the previous night’s murder of the SDPI’s State secretary K.S. Shan at Kuppezham Junction at Mannancherry, Alappuzha, allegedly by Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) activists.
The Sreenivas murder case was investigated by a special team led by then Alappuzha Deputy Superintendent of Police N.R. Jayaraj. Prosecution side was represented by Special Public Prosecutor Prathap G. Padickkal.

title: Ponnam flays BJP for comments on 42% BC quota, says party always favoured capitalists
summary: Ponnam flays BJP for comments on 42% BC quota, says party always favoured capitalists
content:
Senior Congress leader and Transport Minister Ponnam Prabhakar has criticised Telangana BJP leaders, particularly Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy, for ‘commenting’ against the government’s decision to enhance the quota for Backward Classes (BCs) to 42% in proportion to their population.
“BJP was in the forefront in its efforts to dilute the benefits of BCs since the Mandal Commission days, as the party continues to harbour a ‘feudalistic mindset’. The party always worked for the interests of capitalists and never served the interests of BC communities,” he told the media in New Delhi on Friday.
He strongly condemned the remarks made by Mr. Kishan Reddy against the caste survey conducted by the Telangana government, in line with Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s call for “jitni hissedari, utni bhagedari” (benefits in proportion with population).
“BJP announced that a leader from the weaker sections would be made the Chief Minister whenever the party comes to power in Telangana. This promise comes at a time when they did not even make a BC MLA as leader of the legislature party,” he said, adding that Union MoS for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar, who is from the BC community, was removed from the post of Telangana BJP chief.
“N. Ramchander Rao, who fought against the Mandal Commission report, was recently made the State BJP president. And he is questioning the government’s plan to give 42% quota to BCs. Everybody knows that BJP has won the elections in collusion with BRS,” he said, and recalled how Chief Minister A. Revanth reddy had requested Mr. Kishan Reddy to facilitate an appointment with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the interests of the weaker sections but to no avail.
Caste organisations and those who are working for the cause of BCs would not allow BJP leaders into the State if the party continued to oppose BCs. “We have adopted a wait-and-watch approach to ensure that 42% quota for BCs is implemented in the State. BJP leaders should not create obstacles in the process,” he said, and advised the BC leaders in BJP not to toe the line of Mr. Kishan Reddy and Mr. Ramchander Rao.
He reiterated that Congress was committed to social justice and taking steps in that direction. “What did BJP do for BC communities, compared to the efforts put in by Congress?” he asked.

title: Special Intensive Revision is being misused to erase voters of disadvantaged and dissenting communities, says CM Stalin
summary: Tamil Nadu CM M.K. Stalin condemns Bihar voter erasure, warns against threat to democracy by BJP.
content:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and DMK president M.K. Stalin said on Friday that the Special Intensive Revision in Bihar was being misused to quietly erase voters of disadvantaged and dissenting communities, tilting the balance in favour of the BJP. “This is not about reform. It is about engineering outcomes.”
Mr. Stalin, who has been hospitalised since July 21 and underwent angiogram, said, “What happened in Bihar says it all: the Delhi regime knows the same electorate that once voted for it will now vote it out. That is why it is trying to stop them from voting altogether.”
The DMK has been part of the protests in New Delhi against the Special Intensive Revision. “If you cannot defeat us, you seek to delete us. Don’t play with fire. Any threat to our democracy will be met with firm resistance,” he said.
Mr. Stalin further said: “Tamil Nadu will raise its voice with full force. We will fight this injustice with every democratic weapon at our disposal.”
“To every citizen who believes in the Constitution, this is not just about one State, this is about the very foundation of our Republic. Democracy belongs to the people. It will not be stolen,” he said.

title: Telangana moots manufacturing zone, textile clusters for Taiwanese firms
summary: Telangana plans exclusive zones for Taiwanese firms, highlighting textile sector opportunities and industrial growth potential for collaboration.
content:
