Immense significance is attached to the annual event, in which the priests seek forgiveness for all the acts of omissions and commissions, committed knowingly or unknowingly, in the performance of the rituals. Both the senior and junior temple pontiffs, TTD Additional Executive Officer Ch. Venkaiah Chowdary and Deputy EO (temple) Lokanadham were among others present.

title: India to host WHO-IRCH workshop on herbal medicine regulation from August 6
summary: India hosts WHO-IRCH workshop to strengthen global regulation of herbal medicines, featuring collaboration, safety mechanisms, and technical exchange.
content:
India will host the World Health Organization (WHO) - International Regulatory Cooperation for Herbal Medicines (IRCH) workshop from August 6 to 8. Organised by the Ministry of Ayush in collaboration with WHO and supported by the Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H), the three-day international workshop aims to strengthen global capacity in the regulation of herbal medicines.
The workshop is expected to serve as a platform for international cooperation and technical exchange, focusing on five key objectives - fostering collaboration, enhancing safety and efficacy mechanisms, supporting regulatory convergence, and empowering traditional medicine systems globally, an Ayush official said.
Among the highlights are reviews of WHO–IRCH working groups on safety, regulation, efficacy, and intended use of herbal medicines, along with sessions on pre-clinical research, regulatory frameworks, and safety case studies, including a focused discussion on Ashwagandha.
“Participants will benefit from hands-on training in herbal drug identification, heavy metal analysis, and chemo-profiling using HPTLC technology at PCIM&H laboratories. The workshop will also introduce the Ayush Suraksha (Pharmacovigilance) programme, aimed at strengthening safety monitoring of traditional medicines,” the official explained.
To provide exposure to India’s integrative health ecosystem, the delegates will also visit PCIM&H, the National Institute of Unani Medicine (NIUM), Ghaziabad, and the All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi.
With participation from regulatory authorities and experts across continents, the Ministry noted that the workshop is expected to significantly contribute towards harmonising global standards and promoting the safe and effective integration of traditional medicine into mainstream public health systems.

title: Serial conman posing as MP’s son held for cheating hostel owner in Hyderabad
summary: Man posing as VIP and son of TDP MP arrested for cheating hostel owner in Hyderabad
content:
A man posing as a VIP and claiming to be the son of a Member of Parliament from the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) has been arrested by the KPHB police for cheating a women’s hostel owner in Hyderabad.
The accused, 29-year-old Vajila Venkateshwarlu, a native of Guntur district in Andhra Pradesh, who identified himself as Dr. Vikranth Reddy, was arrested near the JNTU traffic signal on August 4, 2025.
According to the police, the complainant — who runs Sitara Women’s PG Hostel opposite the JNTU bus stop in KPHB and also resides there — came into contact with the accused when he visited the hostel under the pretext of helping his cousin and juniors with accommodation.
Over time, he visited the premises on several occasions, even dining there on four separate days, gradually gaining the trust of the complainant.
During one of these interactions, he claimed to own a jewellery shop in Jubilee Hills and convinced her to hand over her gold chain, weighing approximately four tolas, for remodelling. Trusting him, she also paid him ₹55,000 through an online transaction and ₹45,000 in cash after he told her that additional gold was required to complete the design. However, shortly after taking the money and the chain, the accused became unreachable, and his phone was switched off.
Investigation revealed that he has a long history of criminal cases across several police stations in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, including Kavali, Santhapeta, Kakinada Port, Allur, and Jubilee Hills, among others. Offences booked against him range from theft and extortion to cheating and sexual assault. In an earlier instance, he also claimed that he was a neurosurgeon at a reputed hospital in Jubilee Hills. Further investigation is underway.

title: ICCS develops AI-based system to predict rainfall two hours in advance
summary: ICCS develops 'Eye in the Sky' AI platform for real-time rainfall forecasts, aiding disaster preparedness and community safety.
content:
The Institute for Climate Change Studies (ICCS), based in Kottayam, has developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered platform called ‘Eye in the Sky’ ICCS Nowcasting System, designed to deliver real-time rainfall forecasts.
According to an official statement on Tuesday, the system can accurately predict rainfall up to two hours in advance and offers hyper-local insights.
With its high precision, the platform aims at helping communities prepare for sudden and intense downpours. It will also serve as a critical tool for agencies like the Disaster Management Authority, providing timely alerts on heavy rainfall and potential landslides.
A mobile app is being developed to make these updates easily accessible to the public.
The ICCS will showcase this project on August 7 at the Research and Development Summit to be organised by the Kerala State Council for Science, Technology and Environment (KSCSTE) in Thiruvananthapuram.
Operating under the KSCSTE, the ICCS conducts research on the impacts of climate change across various sectors in Kerala, including environment, river basins, and coastal regions. The institute is also planning to collaborate with Kannur University to develop a mini-portable weather station, with a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to be signed soon, said K. Rajendran, Director, ICCS.

title: Bankers told to make adequate security arrangements
summary: Anantapur SP urges banks to enhance security measures as per RBI guidelines, including CCTV installation and cybercrime awareness.
content:
Anantapur Superintendent of Police (SP) P. Jagadeesh asked the bank managements to make adequate security arrangements at the banks as per guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
Mr. Jagadeesh on Tuesday held a meeting with the representatives of banks on the security arrangements to be made at the banks and ATMs. He asked the bank officials to instal CCTVs at the entrance and exit points of the banks to capture people’s movements clearly. The officials were also told to instal latest HD cameras at the ATMs to record the movement of people visiting them day and night. He wanted the data of the recorded footage to be stored in cloud.
The SP said that the windows and grill gates at the banks and ATMs should be strong and added that good quality locks should be used for the shutters. He said that background verification of the outsourced and casual staff who will be employed by the bank shall be done by the police. Further, the SP asked banks to instal alarms that alert the local police station and a designated person of the bank, in case of robbery attempts or any other unforeseen events at the bank.
The SP asked the officials to ensure that the functioning security and fire safety equipment at the banks are periodically inspected and there is adequate lighting near the bank during night. He also wanted the bank officials to educate their customers on cybercrimes, phishing, OTP frauds and other frauds by taking up awareness campaigns. The banks should also display the emergency phone numbers and cybercrime helpline numbers in their premises, the SP said.
Mr. Jagadeesh asked the officials to pass on information about any cybercrime reported by their customers to the tollfree number 1930 immediately. Customers should first report any cybercrime on 1930 and on NCRB portal before approaching the local police, he told the officials. “Lodging a complaint about a cybercrime with the tollfree number immediately will ensure speedy action and justice,” the SP said.
The SP, along with the bank officials, also released a poster to create awareness among the people on cybercrimes during the meeting.

title: Ministry of Ayush releases list of Ayurvedic food preparations under category of ‘Ayurveda Aahara’
summary: FSSAI and Ministry of Ayush release list of Ayurveda Aahara products, promoting traditional dietary wisdom for health and well-being.
content:
Aimed at providing credible reference for the manufacture of Ayurveda Aahara products, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) in consultation with the Ministry of Ayush, has released a list of Ayurvedic food preparations under the category of ‘Ayurveda Aahara’.
Ayurveda Aahara refers to food products developed in line with the holistic dietary principles of Ayurveda. These preparations emphasise balance, seasonal suitability, and using natural ingredients and herbs known for their therapeutic benefits.
With rising public interest in preventive health and sustainable living, Ayurveda Aahara is increasingly recognised as a trusted nutritional choice that harmonises tradition with modern dietary habits, noted a release issued by the Ministry.
“This move will bring India’s traditional food wisdom into the mainstream, following the introduction of the Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahara) Regulations in 2022. These regulations recognise foods based on recipes, ingredients, and processes from authoritative Ayurvedic texts, and the new list brings unprecedented clarity and confidence to consumers and businesses alike,” explained an Ayush Ministry official adding that the list, issued under Note (1) of Schedule B of the regulations, draws directly from classical Ayurvedic texts listed in Schedule A.
To facilitate future additions, FSSAI has established a process for FBOs to request inclusion of additional Category A products not yet listed and such requests need supporting references from authoritative texts in Schedule A. All future updates or changes will be duly notified FSSAI.
Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (I/C), Ministry of Ayush & Minister of State, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, urged citizens to incorporate Ayurveda Aahara into their daily lives to experience its long-term health benefits.
“These are time-tested dietary practices, rooted in India’s traditional wisdom, not only nourish the body but also strengthen immunity, support digestion, and promote overall well-being. In today’s fast-paced lifestyle, adopting Ayurveda Aahara is a meaningful step toward preventive healthcare and a balanced, sustainable way of living,” the Minister said.
Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, stated that the release of the definitive list of Ayurveda Aahara products marks a pivotal step in aligning India’s traditional knowledge systems with modern regulatory frameworks. “This initiative not only empowers Food Business Operators with much-needed clarity but also strengthens consumer trust in Ayurveda-based nutrition,” the Secretary noted.

title: Survey finds 1,365 Nilgiri tahrs in Kerala
summary: Population Estimation 2025, jointly done in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, has pegged the Nilgiri tahr number at 2,668
content:
The joint Nilgiri tahr census in Kerala and Tamil Nadu reported a population of 2,668 Nilgiri tahrs. According to Forest department officials, 1,365 tahr belong to Kerala and 1,303 to Tamil Nadu. The Eravikulam National Park (ENP) is home to the largest contiguous population of Nilgiri tahr in Kerala, numbering 841 individuals.
Officials said that in 2024, the number of tahrs in the ENP was 827. Ninety percent of the tahr population in the State is found in the Munnar landscape alone. A major presence of tahrs in Tamil Nadu is reported in Mukurthi National Park and Grass Hills National Park, lying across the Kerala State border.
The growing tahr population points out the need for interstate cooperation and coordinated management of Nilgiri tahr protected areas.
Thecontrolled burning practice in Eravikulam National Park (ENP)was behind the success of the increasing number of tahrs. According to officials, of the total 1,365 Nilgiri tahrs in the State 1,126 were found in the Munnar landscape. Of this, the ENP is home to 841 tahrs.
Munnar Wildlife Warden K.V. Harikrishnan said the nutritious grasslands of the region are behind the success of the tahr population in the park. “In the nexy three years, controlled burning will be conducted in 97 sq km area of the park.
“The grasslands of ENP become unsuitable for grazing every three years after completing the growth of the natural grass. Nilgiri tahr and other animals will not feed on such grass. Then, controlled burning was introduced in the grasslands of the park on a rotational basis. The practice is conducted after removing all animals from the grasslands,” said Mr. Harikrishnan.
“This year alone, 144 new tahr births were reported in the park. Newborn Nilgiri tahr calves are eating the newly grown grass from the grasslands. Besides ensuring food security for the Nilgiri tahrs, controlled burning also helps increase the productivity of these animals. Nilgiri tahrs are a major prey for tigers and leopards inside the ENP, which in turn helps maintain the population at a controlled level,” said the warden.
The warden stated that the easy availability of prey inside the park has helped lessen the straying of tigers and leopards outside of the park and into human habitat.
The Forest department first took up the controlled burning practice in Eravikulam around 30 years ago, based on the know-how of the Muthuvan tribal communities, said officials.
The joint population estimation of Nilgiri tahrs was conducted continuously for four days in 89 census blocks in Kerala and 182 census blocks in Tamil Nadu. In Kerala, the census was conducted in 19 forest divisions, from Thiruvananthapuram to Wayanad, and all reported the presence of Nilgiri tahr. “The use of standardised techniques such as the ‘Bounded Count and ‘Double Observer’ methods contributed to improved data reliability of the tahr survey,” said an official.
According to officials, historically, Nilgiri tahr occupied a wider range across the Western Ghats, much of which has been lost to plantations, infrastructure development, and land-use change. The Population Estimation 2025 aimed to explore historically known areas and gather information on fragmented tahr populations, as well as the potential for re-establishing habitat connectivity to restore these populations. The survey also discovered the biodiversity richness of tahr habitats, which host apex predators such as the tiger, leopard, and dhole, as well as endemics like the Nilgiri langur and lion-tailed macaque.
Minister for Forests and Wildlife Protection A.K. Saseendran released the census report on Tuesday at Thiruvananthapuram during the 50th anniversary of the establishment of ENP in Munnar.

title: Minister Anagani Satya Prasad inspects fast-track document delivery at Guntur Sub-Registrar office
summary: Minister for Revenue, Registration, and Stamps Anagani Satya Prasad on Tuesday inspected the ongoing pilot project aimed at delivering registered documents within an hour, at the Koritepadu sub-registrar office in Guntur.
content:
Minister for Revenue, Registration, and Stamps Anagani Satya Prasad on Tuesday inspected the ongoing pilot project aimed at delivering registered documents within an hour, at the Koritepadu sub-registrar office in Guntur.
During the visit, officials demonstrated the successful delivery of a registered document in just 15 minutes and 30 seconds, including check slip generation, scanning, and e-KYC.
Commending the staff for their efficiency, the Minister said that the project, also being implemented at three other sub-registrar offices, reflects the government’s commitment to enhancing public service delivery. He highlighted that 13 reforms have been introduced in the Registration Department over the past 13 months since the Coalition government assumed power.
The Minister announced that measures such as slot booking, WhatsApp-based document delivery (over 1.14 lakh documents sent), and auto-mutation in rural and urban areas have been taken to ensure transparency and reduce waiting time. Red cloth podiums have been removed to symbolise equality among citizens, he added.
Mr. Anagani further said that the government has withdrawn the 4% stamp duty on development agreements and reinstated the provision to adjust stamp duty paid during the agreement stage against the final sale deed. For inheritance property certificates, the fee has been made nominal, ₹100 for properties valued below ₹10 lakh and ₹1,000 for higher values.

title: State to develop RRR as six lane road instead of four lane, says R&B Minister
summary: State government to develop Regional Ring Road as six-lane highway, with Minister for Roads & Buildings finalizing plans with Union Minister.
content:
The State government has decided to develop the Regional Ring Road as a six lane one instead of the four lane road proposed earlier.
The government is in the process of modifying the estimates accordingly and tenders are also being finalised in line with the proposed changes, Minister for Roads & Buildings Komatireddy Venkat Reddy said. Mr. Venkat Reddy who called on Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari in New Delhi on Tuesday (August 05) explained about the proposed changes to the latter.
He informed the Union Minister that the State government had completed land acquisition for the northern section of the RRR and requested Mr. Gadkari to start works as early as possible. Mr. Venkat Reddy elaborated on the pending national highway works in Telangana during his meeting with Mr. Gadkari and urged him to ensure conversion of Hyderabad-Vijayawada highway into a six lane road along with service roads.
He took to Mr. Gadkari’s notice the mishap which claimed the lives of two DSP rank officers on the Hyderabad-Vijayawada highway, called as ‘death road’, and Mr. Gadkari reportedly expressed pain at the accident. He assured Mr. Venkat Reddy that the Union Government would approve the expansion of the NH-65 (Hyderabad-Vijayawada highway) during the meeting scheduled on August 15. He asked the State government to finalise the estimates at the earliest so that the Union Ministry could invite tenders for the works.
On the RRR, the Road & B Minister urged the Centre to start works on the northern section with revised estimates within three months. The Union Minister was asked to lay equal emphasis on the southern section and start works on a war footing.
He stressed the need for speedy commencement of works on the RRR southern section which was being developed as an industrial corridor to ensure that land acquisition was competed with the estimated costs as delays in commencement of works could result in escalation of costs in view of the developments planned in the area.
Mr. Gadkari responded positively to the request asking the State government to send proposals pertaining to the alignment speedily so that works could start in the right earnest. Mr. Venkat Reddy also requested the Union Minister to take up works on the five-and-a-half kilometre elevated corridor proposed between Chintalkunta check post and Hayatnagar on the lines of the double-decker corridor of Nagpur.
Mr. Venkat Reddy expressed satisfaction over his meeting with Mr. Gadkari and said the government was in constant touch with the Centre seeking expeditious completion of the highway works.

title: Opposition leader of Thrissur Corporation alleges lapses in canal cleaning works
summary: Leader of the Opposition in Thrissur Corporation alleges corruption in canal cleaning, demands vigilance inquiry into ₹5 crore spending.
content:
Leader of the Opposition of Thrissur Corporation Rajan J. Pallan has raised serious allegations against the corporation, claiming large-scale irregularities in the canal and drain cleaning works undertaken during the monsoon preparedness drive.
Mr. Pallan said that waterlogging even in high-lying areas of the city was primarily due to the corporation’s failure to properly execute pre-monsoon cleaning and the removal of silt from canals. He alleged that more than 200 canal-cleaning projects were marred by corruption, with around ₹5 crore spent this year without ensuring tangible results.
He pointed out that silt removed from the canals in many places was left on the sides without being disposed of, which led to blockages and overflow. Even storm water drains on main roads were not properly desilted, he said.
Several areas in the city experienced flooding following heavy rains, including houses and vehicles near Ashwini Hospital and Bheema Jewellery. The Mundupalam-Avenue Road stretch was submerged and barricaded off due to rising water levels.
Mr. Pallan demanded a vigilance inquiry into the ₹5 crore spent by the corporation on minor and major canal cleaning projects, especially the removal of mud and obstructions from major canals.
He also criticised the corporation for continuing road re-tarring works despite red alert warnings and heavy rain forecasts. Footage of tarring during heavy rain on Marar Road, was aired by media outlets and widely circulated on social media.

title: Lalu's son Tej Pratap announces formation of coalition of 5 minor parties to contest Bihar polls
summary: Tej Pratap Yadav forms coalition of five minor parties to contest Bihar assembly elections, announces candidacy for Mahua seat.
content:
Former Bihar Minister Tej Pratap Yadav on Tuesday (August 5, 2025) announced the formation of a coalition of five minor parties to contest the Assembly elections in the eastern State.
Mr. Yadav,who was recently expelled from RJD by his fatherand party supremo Lalu Prasad, made the announcement at a press conference, which was also attended by the national presidents of the five parties.
The five parties are Vikas Vanchit Insaan Party (VVIP), Bhojpuriya Jan Morcha (BJM), Pragatisheel Janta Party (PJP), Wajib Adhikar Party (WAP) and Sanyukt Kisan Vikas Party (SKVP).
Mr. Yadav said he will contest the Assembly polls, due later this year, from Mahua seat, which he had represented till 2020 before the RJD shifted him to Hasanpur.

title: Heavy rain trigger widespread flooding across Thrissur district
summary: Widespread flooding in Thrissur due to heavy rain, causing damage, evacuations, traffic snarls, and emergency relief efforts initiated.
content:
Widespread flooding has been reported from various parts of Thrissur following heavy rain that lashed the district on Monday(August 4, 2025), with several residential areas submerged and daily life thrown into chaos. Localities including Saktan Nagar, M.G. Road, Aquatic complex line, and Paliyam road, Ikkanda Warrier Road and North bus stand area in the city experienced severe waterlogging.
In Aquatic line, floodwaters entered several homes, causing significant damage to household appliances and furniture. Many families were evacuated and shifted to safer locations. Although these areas witnessed flooding last year as well, residents say that it only took two hours of rain this time for water to enter their homes. Residents blamed flawed drainage systems and canal blockages for the recurring issue.
Chelakkara, Palappilly, Puthur, Vettukadu, and Ezhamkallu also reported flooding in residential areas, leaving roads there submerged. Waterlogging at Mulangunnathukavu on Thrissur-Shoranur Road  led to traffic snarls. The heavy rainfall also exposed numerous potholes on roads, increasing the risk of accidents.
Fishing boats that ventured into the sea defying the warning were caught in rough winds around 8 a.m. but managed to return safely to the Munakkakadavu Harbour and other nearby shelters.
In Pothan Chira, six houses were reportedly flooded. The downpour also triggered gushing of water from a nearby rubber estate into the surrounding houses in Palappilly. Varantarappalli witnessed waterlogging in multiple areas as the rain intensified.
Meanwhile, in response to the severe rain-related damages reported in Puthur grama panchayat over the last two days, Revenue Minister K. Rajan convened an emergency meeting to assess the situation. The Minister announced that round-the-clock control rooms have been set up at the Thrissur Taluk Office and the Puthur panchayat. For emergencies, residents can contact the Thrissur taluk emergency operations centre at 0487-2331443.
Instructions were given to ensure the readiness of ambulances, the fire force, electricity, and Irrigation departments. To support immediate relief efforts, ₹1 lakh has been sanctioned for the procurement of emergency equipment, and an additional ₹1 lakh for setting up relief camps.
The Minister directed the DFO to immediately remove fallen trees and instructed the panchayat secretary to take steps under the Disaster Management Act to cut down trees that pose a threat to public safety. To ease water flow near Ezhamkallu Church, the canal was deliberately breached. At the Puthur Zoological Park, canal blockages will be cleared urgently, as per instructions given to the Zoo Director.

title: Narcotics sniffer dog detects 30kgs ganja at Vijayawada railway station
summary: The sniffer dog squad in a joint operation with GRP, RPF, and CIB seized 30 kgs ganja worth ₹1.5 lakh from three women on board Chennai-bound Shalimar-Chennai Coromandel Express at Vijayawada railway station.
content:
The sniffer dog squad in a joint operation with Government Railway Police (GRP), Railway Protection Force (RPF), and Crime Intelligence Branch (CIB) seized 30 kgs ganja worth ₹1.5 lakh from three women on board Chennai-bound Shalimar-Chennai Coromandel Express at Vijayawada railway station.
The arrested smugglers were identified as Susanthi, Pushpa Latha, and Manisha, all natives of Nabarangpur in Odisha, said Railway Central Intelligence Branch (CIB) Inspector K. Madhusudhan, who headed the operation.
“During surprise raids on the halted trains at Vijayawada railway station on Monday (August 5, 2025), dog Leo, an expert in narcotics detection, pounced on the stocks concealed in the coach, and alerted the RPF and GRP personnel,” said inspector M.V. Durga Rao, Inspector of Railway Police (Lines).
During questioning, the women smugglers said that a man identified as Bola handed over three bags containing ganja (Cannabis) to them at Visakhapatnam station.
A case has been registered under NDPS Act, and other charges. The accused along with the seized ganja have been produced in the court, Mr. Madhusudhan said.

title: KSRTC employees’ strike: Several commuters turn to private buses in Shivamogga, many cancel plans
summary: KSRTC employees' strike in Shivamogga prompts mixed response, with officials operating buses using trainee staff members.
content:
The KSRTC employees’ strike received a mixed response in Shivamogga on Tuesday. While the employees did not turn up for the duty, the KSRTC officials did operate a few buses deploying the trainee staff members.
The passengers who reached the bus stand in the morning with no information about the strike were in shock. A majority of them moved to the private bus stand, while a few returned home, cancelling their travel plan for the day. The Joint Action Committee (JAC) of the employees has decided to call off the strike, bringing relief to the passengers.
The officers of the corporation did manage to run the buses to taluk centres from Shivamogga by deploying trainee drivers and conductors on duty, as the regular employees were on strike.
The passengers had services to taluk centres – Sagar, Bhadravathi, and Honnali and a few other centres. However, there was no service to Bengaluru. The passengers were dependent on the private buses to reach the capital. Those who were planning to travel to coastal area opted for private buses.
Mahadevu, office-bearer of KSRTC Employees Union, said that across the State, 1.15 lakh employees were on strike. However, the officers had put the trainee staff on the job forcibly. “We want the officers to stop pressurising the employees. If any employee is willing to drive buses, let them do it voluntarily,” he said.
Meanwhile, T.R. Naveen Kumar, Divisional Controller of KSRTC (Shivamogga), said that the officers did not force any staff. “Some drivers and conductors have come forward to work voluntarily. We are hopeful that the employees will return to duty,” the officer said.

title: KKRTC bus services hit in Yadgir as employees strike work
summary: Partial response to transport corporation strike in Raichur, good response in Yadgir; KKRTC employees resume night duties.
content:
The strike call given by the Joint Action Committee (JAC) of road transport corporation employees demanding payment, pending arrears and a wage hike received partial response in Raichur district, while it was good in Yadgir district.
Both districts are served by the Kalyana Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (KKRTC).
According to Divisional Controller in Raichur district Chandrasekhar, bus services were not affected much as expected. Though buses were operated, their numbers were few compared to services run on a normal day.
A passenger waits for bus service to resume in Yadgir on Tuesday.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
Out of the scheduled 398 bus departures, only 195 buses were operated from 5.30 a.m. to 4 p.m., touching 49%.
“Bus services from Raichur to Mantralayam in Andhra Pradesh, Sindhanur and other important centres were not affected. We operated buses even in local areas,” he added.
Meanwhile, in Yadgir district, the strike call received a good response. According to Divisional Controller Sunil Kumar Chandaragi, only 23 buses out of the 214 scheduled departures were operated.
Passengers were seen struggling to find transportation in many rural areas in Yadgir district and even in the district headquarters.
Private vehicles operated services from the Central Bus Stand to various parts in the district, including Gurmitkal, Shahapur, Shorapur and Wadagera, and also Narayanpet in Andhra Pradesh.
There were no reports of untoward incidents in both these districts, except disruption in bus services.
And, KKRTC employees decided to attend to their night duties on Tuesday itself in view of a direction from the High Court of Karnataka, sources said.

title: Hectic road digging creates blockade for commuters
summary: GHMC digs up roads for storm water drains despite heavy rainfall predictions, causing daily traffic congestion in Hyderabad.
content:
Predictions of heavy to very heavy rainfall in the month of August have done nothing to dampen the digging drive of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC). After biding time the entire summer, the contractors of the Strategic Nala Development Programme have now started digging up roads and road margins to lay storm water drains. This digging activity has turned traffic congestion into a daily problem for commuters.
At Chintalkunta Y junction near LB Nagar, the road digging started about a month ago, to lay storm water pipelines along the RTC Colony main road. The project began while a ban on road cutting was in place in view of rains.
Now, the route has been rendered unusable for vehicles, especially four-wheelers, on the connecting road towards the Sagar Ring Road. The deep trenches for laying 900 mm pipes has also restricted movement on the flyover from Bairamalguda towards LB Nagar Junction, and to proceed on the Inner Ring Road (IRR) towards Nagole. Also out of bounds for many vehicles is the Chintalkunta underpass landing on National Highway 65.
Residents of several colonies around Jahangir Nagar, RTC Colony, Venkata Ramana Colony, and Padmavathi Colony are bearing the brunt of the ongoing digging work.
“In the absence of the Chintalkunta underpass, to get to the other side of the road, we need to take a round about either from the Vanasthalipuram side or travel up to LB Nagar junction, both of which increase the fuel cost tremendously. This has become a pain on a daily basis,” complained M. Srinivas Rao, a working professional who resides in Venkata Ramana Colony.
For the commuters to Nagole, it is even more cumbersome as it adds up to over two kilometres up to the IRR, costing not only fuel, but extra time too during peak hours.
Locals vouch that the RTC Colony main road was laid two to three years ago. While a cement concrete road is built with a lifespan of a minimum of 10 years, this road has been dug up much ahead of time, due to the absence of drainage.
“Every time it rains, the road gets filled with flood water from all the surrounding colonies, making it difficult for pedestrians to negotiate their way. Last time it was re-laid, they did not bother to provide for storm water drainage. There were only sewerage lines to take in the flood water too, and it was a problem. Now, they are breaking the road to lay the drains,” related Abdul Lateef (name changed), a shopkeeper on the road.

title: MITS named best engineering college in A.P.
summary: MITS named "Best Engineering College - 2024" by ISTE-A.P., with students earning State honors for excellence. Award ceremony on August 14.
content:
The Madanapalle Institute of Technology and Science (MITS) was named the “Best Engineering College – 2024” by the Indian Society for Technical Education, Andhra Pradesh section (ISTE-A.P.) for excellence in academics, research, and institutional performance.
The award will be presented at the ISTE student convention on August 14 at MITS. Two students also earned State honours — Kagithi Bhargavi (EEE) as best electrical and electronics engineering student and Karthik Kovi (CSE) as best student innovator. MITS leaders thanked ISTE-A.P. and lauded the students’ achievements.

title: KSRTC services return to normal in Mysuru after union calls off strike
summary: KSRTC bus services in Mysuru disrupted by strike, gradually returning to normal with partial operations and alternative transport options.
content:
KSRTC bus services, which were disrupted in Mysuru due to an indefinite strike by employees on Tuesday, are gradually returning to normal following the decision by the Joint Action Committee (JAC) of transport corporation employees to call it off.
Soon after the decision, buses began leaving depots and arriving at the KSRTC’s suburban bus stand here to ferry commuters to their respective destinations.
“Employees have started reporting to work (following the developments). However, full-scale operations are expected to resume only by Wednesday morning. Night service buses and some scheduled routes were operated in the evening,” said KSRTC Divisional Controller (rural) Srinivas.
Earlier in the day, around 60% of services were hit by the strike. Newly-appointed and contractual drivers managed to operate a few routes, but the services remained inadequate for the volume of passengers. Many commuters were seen waiting at the bus stand, hoping for a ride.
Out of the 750 buses usually operated daily in the Mysuru Rural KSRTC Division, only 200 were on the road—and only on select routes, with all other buses going off the roads. To manage the crisis, private bus operators were permitted to run services from the suburban bus stand.
The Divisional Controller toldThe Hinduthat services were partially impacted and that 100 trainee drivers and 170 contract drivers were deployed to operate on essential routes. “Since they are not part of the strike, they reported for duty,” he noted.
As an alternative arrangement, a meeting was convened by the Deputy Commissioner, Superintendent of Police, and Regional Transport Officers to ensure private buses operated to mitigate the strike’s impact. Later in the day, the suburban bus stand wore a deserted look as passengers opted for alternative modes of transport—including railways—to reach their destinations, with not many buses available for rides.
Mr. Srinivas said there were no takers for buses bound for Bengaluru—especially electric and air-conditioned buses—in the morning, as news of the strike had already spread. “While we couldn’t operate all scheduled services, we ensured that major routes were covered,” he added.
Reports from various taluks indicated that many passengers were left stranded due to the sudden disruption in public transport. In Mysuru city, the strike caused severe inconvenience to intra-city commuters, many of whom were left waiting at the city bus stand.
The demand for autorickshaws and cab services surged following the strike. Long queues of commuters were also seen at the pre-paid auto kiosks outside the city railway station.

title: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Minister Atchannaidu assures uninterrupted supply of fertilizers to farmers for kharif
summary: Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Minister Atchannaidu assures uninterrupted supply of fertilizers to farmers for kharif. Directing officials to monitor the supply and prevent shortages, Atchannaidu terms YSRCP’s allegations as false.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu has assured farmers that the government will ensure uninterrupted fertilizer supply throughout the kharif season.
Addressing a teleconference with the district Collectors and agriculture officials on Tuesday, Mr. Atchannaidu directed the officials to monitor the supply and prevent shortages, especially in the cooperative societies and Markfed depots.
“No farmer should face inconvenience in accessing fertilizers, and officials should monitor every cooperative society and ensure supplies are being distributed fairly,” he said.
Taking note of the media reports of urea shortage in certain areas and seeking a detailed report of them, he said the government had secured a higher quantity of fertilizers through proactive coordination with the Agriculture Ministry.
Dismissing reports of shortage as false propaganda by the YSRCP, Mr. Atchannaidu said  15.94 LMT of fertilizers had already been made available — 8.91 LMT sold and 7.03 LMT in stock. “Any dealer creating artificial scarcity, or selling above MRP will face strict action,” the Minister warned.
“The government is also introducing nano urea and nano DAP, which can meet 25% of nutrient requirements,” Mr. Atchannaidu said. Referring to efforts made by the government to expedite allocations from the Centre, he said fresh supply of 4.58 LMT for August had been approved.

title: PM to inaugurate extended Vande Bharat train service from Belagavi on Sunday
summary: Prime Minister Modi virtually inaugurates Belagavi-Bengaluru Vande Bharat Express extension, enhancing connectivity in Karnataka.
content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Belagavi-Bengaluru Vande Bharat Express virtually on Sunday. The train now running between Dharwad and Bengaluru has been extended till Belagavi.
Minister Pralhad Joshi and MPs Jagadish Shettar and Eeranna Kadadi have thanked the Prime Minister. They said they had earlier submitted requests for the extension of the service.
The train will leave Belagavi at 5.20 a.m. and reach Bengaluru by 1.50 p.m. It will leave Bengaluru by 2.20 p.m. and reach Belagavi by 10.40 p.m.
This service will increase connectivity between Bengaluru, Tumakuru, Davangere, Haveri, Hubballi, Dharwad and Belgaum, Mr. Joshi said.
It is expected to run six days a week, though a final timetable is yet to be released.
Mr. Shettar thanked the Prime Minister for the train. “I have been following it up since I became MP. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw gave in-principle for the train a few months ago. However, the movement was delayed as coaches were not ready. In my meeting with the Prime Minister, I requested for the train service. He assured me he will instruct the Minister and officials concerned. Officers have now confirmed the run of the extended service,” Mr. Shettar told reporters in New Delhi on Tuesday.

title: Sponsor claims Argentinian Football Association has not yet officially called off Kerala tour
summary: Argentinian Football Association's potential tour to Kerala in question due to contract disputes, creating disappointment among fans.
content:
The Argentinian Football Association (AFA) has not yet officially denied to tour Kerala during the October-November window this year and if the AFA violates the contract to that effect then it will amount to cheating, which will be dealt with legally, says Anto Augustine, managing director of the Kochi-based broadcasting company, which claims to be the sponsors of the proposed tour.
He was addressing a press conference here on Tuesday after Sports Minister V. Abdurahiman said the previous day that the visit of the Argentina national team to Kerala was off.  This had created much heartburn among football fans across the State.
Mr. Augustine claimed that his company had already paid the AFA over ₹130 crore based on a contract that the same Argentina team, including Lionel Messi, that won the last World Cup would play two matches and participate in a fans meeting during the tour.
“But now the association has informed that the team will visit the State in September 2026 and sent a draft contract to sign if that is acceptable to us. It has also proposed to send a delegation to discuss the matter, both of which are not acceptable to us,” he said.
He said that a contract already signed, based on which payment had been made after informing the State government, Centre, Finance Ministry, and the Reserve Bank of India, cannot be revised just like that.
“Our contract was that the same team that won the last World Cup will play in Kerala. By next September, the World Cup will be over and there is no guarantee that Argentina will win it again. We will wait for another 15 days for a confirmation since making the infrastructure arrangements will take time and cannot be done in short notice,” said Mr. Augustine, who wondered whether the AFA, having realised the potential of the tour, was trying to bargain.
The Sports Minister had announced last November that the Argentina national football team featuring Messi would play two exhibition matches against Japan and Qatar in Kerala in 2025. However, when the itinerary was released by the AFA this May, there wasn’t a stopover in Kerala. The blame was then put on the Kochi-based company as the Minister said it was for the company, which had an agreement with the AFA, to explain. However, in June, Mr. Abdurahiman raised fresh hopes through his social media  post, “Messi is coming.”

title: Chittoor district administration geared up for Kanipakam Brahmotsavams
summary: Chittoor District gears up for 21-day 'Brahmotsavams' at Kanipakam temple with extensive arrangements and security measures.
content:
The district administration is all geared up for the smooth conduct of the 21-day ‘Brahmotsavams’ at the Sri Varasiddhi Vinayaka Swamy temple in Kanipakam, which would be held from August 27 to September 16.
Chittoor District Collector Sumit Kumar on Tuesday held a meeting on the arrangements to be made for the event with Superintendent of Police (SP) V.N. Manikanta Chandolu, temple executive officer (EO) Penchala Kishore, Putalapattu MLA K. Murali Mohan and others. Mr. Sumit Kumar said that a coordination committee led by the temple EO with officials of Revenue, Police, Panchayat Raj, Medical and Health and other departments has been formed. The committee was asked to formulate an action plan for the event, he added.
The Collector asked the EO, officials of Electricity and Fire Services departments to inspect the power supply situation inside and outside the temple, and ensure that there are no lapses. He asked the officials concerned to remove the bushes on both sides of the road from Chittoor to Kanipakam.
Mr. Sumit Kumar also asked the Medical and Health Department to make available expert doctors, medical camps and ambulances to meet any emergencies. The Panchayat officials were asked to maintain hygienic conditions near the temple, set up mobile toilets and make provision for providing safe drinking water to the devotees.
The Collector added that Vinayaka Chavithi falling on August 27, Radhotsavam on September 3, Pushpa Pallaki on September 13, Teppotsavam on September 16 will attract huge devotees and asked officials to make fool-proof arrangements to meet the devotee rush. He wanted more RTC buses to the temple town for the convenience of the devotees.
Meanwhile, the SP said that a Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) rank official would head the security arrangements and CCTV surveillance will be in place for the entirety of the festivities, especially on Radhotsavam day. Focus would be on security in the temple premises, mandapam, Koneru, parking areas and bus stand. A helpdesk will also be set up and the arrangements would be monitored 24X7 through the command control centre, he said.
Police will use two drones to monitor the security, the SP said, and asked the temple management to use another two drones for surveillance. He also asked the temple officials to make necessary announcements through the public address system. Consumption of liquor would be prohibited in the areas nearby the temple, while steps would be taken to control the sale of liquor after 8 p.m., he said. The SP asked officials to make available a fire tender for responding quickly to any fire mishaps.
Mr. Murali Mohan said that arrangements will be made in coordination with 20 other departments for the smooth conduct of the event. He stressed on maintaining queue lines in a proper manner to provide hassle-free darshan to the devotees.

title: Man arrested for burgling brother’s house in Mysuru’s Nanjangud
summary: Man arrested for burgling brother's house, stealing gold jewelry and cash; confesses to crime, items recovered, remanded in custody.
content:
A man in Nanjangud has been arrested for allegedly burgling his brother’s house and stealing 90g of gold jewellery and ₹5.15 lakh in cash fromt there.
According to the police, the accused, identified as Rajendra, reportedly confessed to the crime during the interrogation. The stolen items and cash was recovered from the accused, the police said.
The police said that Sannathayamma of Madakehundi village of Nanjangud taluk had lodged a complaint with the jurisdictional Hullahalli police station on July 7, stating that her house had been burgled when she was away working in the field. Upon her return, she found that  90g of gold jewellery and ₹5.15 lakh kept in the house was missing. She suspected burglars had gained entry into the house by removing the roof tiles.
A crime detection team of Mysuru district police arrested Ms. Sannathayamma’s brother-in-law, Rajendra, on August 3.
The accused was produced before the court and remanded in judicial custody.

title: State govt. will continue talks with Governor: Bindu
summary: The Left Democratic Front government is reportedly planning to resume its efforts to reach a consensus with Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arleker, also the Chancellor of State-run universities, over various issues concerning the higher education sector.
content:
The Left Democratic Front government is reportedly planning to resume its efforts to reach a consensus with Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arleker, also the Chancellor of State-run universities, over various issues concerning the higher education sector.
Higher Education Minister R. Bindu, who, along with Industries Minister P. Rajeeve called on Mr. Arlekar on August 3, told the media here on Tuesday that the talks had been inconclusive. “We will meet the Governor again. Last time, we spoke with him for about one-and-a-half hours. However, Mr. Rajeeve and I had to rush to Ernakulam to pay tributes to critic and writer M.K. Sanoo,” she said. Ms. Bindu said that another round of talks would be held in the coming days, but the schedule had not been fixed.
Meanwhile, Ms. Bindu supported General Education Minister V. Sivankutty’s proposal to do away with the practice of having “back benches” in school classrooms. She said that such a move would help the teachers view all students without any pre-conceived notions. It could also lead to the students actively participating in the classroom sessions. Asked if the colleges in the State could also follow the practice, she said that the respective authorities might have to take a call on it.

title: Guntur Commissioner cracks the whip on ward secretaries
summary: Guntur Municipal Commissioner Puli Srinivasulu on Tuesday issued stern warnings to ward secretaries who were absent during working hours without prior approval or notice.
content:
Guntur Municipal Commissioner Puli Srinivasulu on Tuesday issued stern warnings to ward secretaries who were absent during working hours without prior approval or notice.
During a surprise inspection on Tuesday (August 5, 2025) at several ward secretariats, including those near Sanakkayala Factory, Kugler Hospital Road, and Gunturuvari Thota, the Commissioner expressed serious displeasure over negligence of duty by the staff.
Show-cause notices have been issued to secretaries after offices were found locked or unmanned during official hours. In several cases, officials had failed to sign the attendance register and left the office. He directed the concerned staff to report and explain their absence in person and warned that departmental action would be taken against those who neglect their duties.
Mr. Srinivasulu emphasised that all secretaries must strictly follow working hours, remain available to the public, and be accountable. He further said that daily surprise checks will be conducted going forward. Any official going out for government work or surveys must record it properly, and leave must be sanctioned only through the nodal or departmental officer.

title: Priyank Kharge, Sharan Prakash Patil accused of ignoring demands of Ediga community
summary: Pranavananda Swami urges CM Siddaramaiah to address Ediga community's demands, warns of new political party formation.
content:
National president of the Arya Ediga Kendra Samiti and Peethadhipathi of Brahmashree Narayana Guru Shakti Peetha at Kardal village in Kalaburagi district Pranavananda Swami has urged Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Priyank Kharge to lead a delegation of Ediga community leaders to Chief Minister Siddaramaiah urging him to consider the long-pending demands of the community.
Addressing presspersons in Kalaburagi on Monday, the swamiji recalled that Mr. Kharge and Medical Education Minister Sharan Prakash Patil visited the community’s protest venue and expressed their solidarity when he launched an indefinite hunger strike in Kalaburagi in 2022 demanding the then BJP government to fulfill their demands. But now both Mr. Kharge and Dr. Patil have turned a deaf ear to the community’s long-pending demands, he said.
Their demands included lifting a ban on toddy tapping, providing two acres of land for cultivation to each Ediga family, allocating ₹500 crore funds to the Brahmashree Narayana Guru Corporation for the welfare of Ediga and Billava communities, installation of a Sri Narayana Guru statue in front of the Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru, establishment of study centres in the names of Sri Narayana Guru and Hendada Marayya in the Gulbarga University and also celebrating the birth anniversary of 12th century social reformer Hendada Marayya as a State function.
Accusing the Siddaramaiah-led State government of discriminating against the community by inducting only one legislator belonging to the Ediga community into the Cabinet, the seer demanded that the State government induct one more legislator from the community into the Cabinet. If the State government continues to neglect the demands of the Ediga community, prominent leaders from the community will float a new political party in the State, he said.
Accusing political parties of misusing youths as tools of violence in the name of caste and religion to disrupt peace in society, the swamiji appealed to the youths of Ediga community to stay away from such harmful influences. He urged the youths of Ediga community to follow the ideologies of Sri Narayana Guru and contribute to society’s progress.

title: Rethinking classroom seating desirable, but question mark over practicality of U-shaped classrooms
summary: Educationists advocate for rethinking classroom seating arrangements to enhance student-teacher engagement, but practical implementation poses challenges.
content:
Minister for General Education V. Sivankutty’s proposal to reconfigure classrooms to prevent students from being pushed to the back benches has been largely welcomed though questions remain about its practicality.
Educationist R.V.G. Menon says rethinking the classroom seating arrangement is desirable, especially if it brings all students face to face with teachers. The traditional row upon row seating style is an unwritten rule in schools that is best avoided. The shift away from it will help promote closer engagement and give and take between students and teachers. “The most important thing is flexibility in the classroom environment. Teachers should be free to make any amendments,” he says.
He, however, acknowledges that it is very difficult to change the existing configuration as it depends on the student strength and classroom size.
All Kerala School Teachers’ Union (AKSTU) general secretary O.K. Jayakrishnan says reworking classroom seating will promote inclusivity and ensure individual attention to students. However, its practical implementation across classes will be difficult.
It is well suited to primary classrooms that usually have 10-20 students. However, in high school and higher secondary classes, the large number of students and the classroom dimensions will likely not prove conducive to any shift in the seating pattern, he says.
Though the model to be adopted in the State was yet to finalised, Ranjith Unnikrishnan, consultant orthopaedic spine surgeon at KIMS Health here, warns against the U-shaped or horseshoe-shaped seating arrangement that is gaining popularity. “Such a model will lead to neck pain. Classrooms should resemble an amphitheatre, with both the students in the front row and the back able to look straight.”
He calls for deciding the maximum seating capacity first and then deciding the size of the room based on various dimensions instead of the other way around.
Ophthalmologist George Thomas is of the same view. Even if students in the middle in the U or semi-circle model are able to look straight ahead, those sitting at the two extremities in such a model will end up with neck pain or headache if they have to twist their neck to look at a screen or white/blackboard for prolonged periods such as in Mathematics or Science periods.
Moreover, a proper distance from the screen/board will have to be ensured for students sitting at the two ends.
Sunitha G.S., a Class III teacher at Government Model Lower Primary School, Thycaud, says this model works for younger students since they do not have to look at the board for long stretches; most of the learning is activity-based which children enjoy when the teacher was in their midst. Also, it is fit for a classroom that has around 25 children. Her students keep rotating their seats too.
However, arranging furniture in such a pattern for upper primary or other older students could be a problem, she points out.

title: Railways mounts vigil on errant staff to curb insider role in sabotage
summary: Indian Railways increases surveillance on employees to prevent sabotage, focusing on contractual staff and enhancing security measures.
content:
The Indian Railways has upped vigil on employees, including contractual staff engaging in undesirable activities to prevent possible sabotage in train operations.
Responding to an alert issued by the Commissioner of Railway Safety (CRS) on the possibility of sabotage involving insiders, the Railway Board in a written communication said the Railway Security Management System, which tracked individuals engaging in undesirable activities, was being actively updated by all Zonal Railways.
The railways is the largest national transporter, which employs over 12 lakh employees across its network. A sizeable number of contractual staff are also being involved in maintenance, catering, house-keeping and other activities.
After anin-depth investigation into the rear-collision of Train 12578 Musiri-Dharbanga Bagmati Expressat Kavarapettai in Southern Railway on the night of October 11, 2024, the CRS in his final report concluded that the accident was caused by sabotage.
Saying that the possibility of an insider playing a role in the sabotage was a grave matter, he wrote to the Railway Board suggesting that the intelligence wing of the railways should develop a method of gathering inputs on such potential threats.
In a reply to the CRS, a copy of which was marked to General Managers, Principal Chief Safety Officers and Principal Chief Security Commissioners of all Zonal Railways, the Railway Board said the Special Intelligence Branch of the Railway Protection Force was instructed “to intensify intelligence gathering on railway employees, contractual workers and associated personnel. Proactive measures like scenario-based training, mock drills, and deployment of special teams are in place to detect threats and protect railway infrastructure effectively.”
The post-accident investigation report also called for reviewing the engagement and exposure of contractual staff for the maintenance and operation of critical safety features and systems and allowing them to developing skills in those areas. Such a practice should be reviewed in priority and cut short to minimal in short term and null in long term, the report said.
Asked about the progress of investigation in the Bagmati Express accident, especially in the backdrop of the CRS confirming sabotage, a Southern Railway spokesperson said the case was under investigation by the Government Railway Police. Vulnerable areas prone to sabotage were identified and the process of installing CCTV in those sections was underway.

title: KTU decides to waive year-out system for UG programmes this year
summary: KTU waives year-out system, minimum credit requirements for undergraduate programmes due to student representation and protests.
content:
APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University (KTU) has decided to waive the year-out system for all undergraduate programmes for the present academic year.
The minimum credit requirement for promotion to the fifth and seventh semesters has been waived following representations from student organisations and affiliated colleges. The issue, which potentially affected several students under the 2019 regulations, had triggered protests recently.
Students were required to earn a minimum of 21 out of 38 credits from the first two semesters to be eligible for promotion to the fifth semester and 47 out of 82 credits from the first four semesters to advance to the seventh semester.
While these criteria had been temporarily suspended during the COVID-19 pandemic, they were reinstated in the 2023-24 academic year. However, this year, the university received numerous petitions from stakeholders, citing the difficulties faced by a substantial number of students who remain ineligible for promotion due to credit shortfalls.
An analysis by the KTU’s Academics Branch revealed that around 4,208 BTech students at present fell short of the required credits for seventh-semester registration. Besides, 6,428 students were ineligible for the fifth semester. These figures represent nearly 15% and 20% from the respective BTech batches.
Students unable to progress to the fifth semester would require to transition to the revised 2024 curriculum, leading to additional academic burden due to transitory course requirements.
The university also found that students from other undergraduate programmes face similar risks of losing academic continuity due to unmet credit requirements.
The decision to waive the minimum credit requirement for promotion to the higher semesters will be subsequently reported at the upcoming meetings of the Academic Council and the Board of Governors.

title: PM Modi compliments Amit Shah for becoming longest-serving Union Home Minister
summary: PM Modi praises Amit Shah for becoming longest-serving Home Minister, highlighting key decisions and achievements under his leadership.
content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday (August 5, 2025) praised Union Home Minister Amit Shah for becoming the longest-serving incumbent in his Ministry.
In his address to the National Democratic Alliance’s parliamentary party group, Mr. Modi noted that Mr. Shah has become the longest serving Home Minister, overtaking Bharatiya Janata Party veteran L. K. Advani, a co-founder of the group in 1998. “It is just the beginning,” he said, adding that there was a long way to go.
Mr. Shah has been at the helm since the Modi government took over for the second time in 2019, and his stint so far is of six years and 65 days. His tenure has been marked by several key decisions, such asthe abrogation of Article 370, and actions on the internal security front, including a series of successful anti-Maoist operations.
The Union Home Minister also received compliments from his Cabinet and party colleagues. Congratulating him, Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said: “...you have achieved a historic milestone. This historic achievement was recorded today, on August 5. On a similar historic day, August 5, 2019, you announced the abrogation of Article 370 in Parliament, adding a new chapter to India’s history.”
“Under your leadership, India has dealt a decisive blow to Maoism and taken historic decisions likethe Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA). Your unwavering commitment to national security has further strengthened the confidence and pride of the nation’s people. Your foresight, determination, and decisions taken in the interest of the nation are commendable. Wishing you abundant success, glory, and a long-lasting public life filled with numerous achievements,” he said through his X handle.
Speaking with the media, BJP MP Jagdambika Pal said Mr. Shah had taken historic decisions, including the abrogation of Article 370 and Article 35A, under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi.
Via his X handle, the party’s IT cell in-charge Amit Malviya said: “Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s tenure has been marked by bold, historic decisions -- from the abrogation of Article 370 to a firm crackdown on terrorism and strengthening of internal security.”

title: Young scientists told to ‘co-create’ with farmers at IISER Tirupati
summary: Samir Somaiya urges India to shift to a 'soil-based' economy, emphasizing environmental conservation and integration of modern and traditional practices.
content:
Samir Somaiya, chairman and managing director of Godavari Biorefineries Limited and Chancellor of Somaiya Vidyavihar University called for the urgent transition of India from an ‘oil-based’ economy to a ‘soil-based’ one. An expert in biorefining, Mr. Somaiya’s observation came as a clarion call towards conserving the environment.
Delivering the chief guest’s address at the sixth convocation of Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER), Tirupati, on Tuesday, he encouraged the young scientists to ‘co-create’ with farmers, hinting at the need to adopt an approach that integrated modern agricultural practices with traditional wisdom. Mr. Somaiya spoke on the importance of knowing one’s heritage and its connection to scientific pursuits.
Jhillu Singh Yadav, Chairperson, Board of Governors, IISER, called upon the graduates to transform into catalysts for change, urging them to tackle pressing issues in agriculture, sustainable chemistry and the manufacturing of semi-conductors and enzymes.
His emphasis was on identifying manufacturing processes that do not pollute the environment, stating that such innovations would help in the nation’s advancement. Referring to ‘Viksit Bharat’, he called upon the graduates to become ‘good scientists’ and use their knowledge for the country’s development.
IISER Director Santanu Bhattacharya gave away 22 PhDs, eight Integrated PhDs, three MS degrees, 141 flagship BSMS dual degrees, 69 professional Master’s degrees, six BS degrees and six B.Sc degrees. The convocation concluded with a unique trilingual vote of thanks delivered by the Registrar Inderpreet Singh Kohli in Hindi, Telugu and English.

title: Yellow Line Metro project belongs to people, not to any political party or govt. alone: DKS
summary: Deputy CM Shivakumar emphasizes Bengaluru Metro as a joint effort, urges Opposition to avoid credit politics.
content:
Deputy Chief Minister and Bengaluru Development Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Tuesday emphasised that the Bengaluru Metro project is a collaborative effort between the Union and State governments, and asked the Opposition to not make it a subject of “credit politics.”
His comments came after he conducted an inspection of the Yellow Line Metro ahead of its inauguration by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, scheduled for August 10.
Speaking to reporters after his inspection of the 19.15-km Yellow Line corridor, Mr. Shivakumar stressed that the project belongs to the people of the city, not to any political party or government alone.
“The Metro project is not solely a Union government initiative. It is a joint partnership between the State and Union governments. The focus here is on serving the people, not credit politics,” he said.
Responding to questions about who initiated the Metro’s inauguration, Mr. Shivakumar clarified, “The Chief Minister and I had requested the Prime Minister to inaugurate it. He has now given time. This is not just a Union government project, both governments have a 50:50 partnership. If they have a chairman on their side, we have a managing director on ours. No one has exclusive authority here.”
The Yellow Line, connecting R.V. Road to Bommasandra, has been constructed at a cost of ₹7,610 crore and features 16 stations. “A small, simple function will be held at the IIMB auditorium that day. The Prime Minister, Chief Minister, and MLAs will travel by Metro during the event,” Mr. Shivakumar said. He added that the State will also submit a request to the Prime Minister for additional funds required for land acquisition for the proposed double-decker flyover project.
Taking a dig at BJP MPs, the Deputy Chief Minister said, “If the MPs who are now creating a ruckus help get some funds sanctioned, it would be great for Bengaluru. Not a single one of them is talking about funding. They only point out faults.” He said the State is planning to integrate double-decker flyovers wherever Metro lines are built, and that both BBMP and BMRCL will work jointly on land acquisition and compensation.
He also took a swipe at MP for Bengaluru South Tejasvi Surya, who had been protesting against the State government to open the Yellow Line at the earliest, saying, “He is a young man in a hurry, but he lacks experience. These projects cannot be rushed,” he said.
Mr. Shivakumar informed that three trains have already arrived for the Yellow Line, with the fourth expected in August. “It takes about a week to begin operations after a train arrives. Initially, three trains will run at 25-minute intervals. As more trains arrive, frequency will increase to 20 minutes and eventually to 10 minutes.”
To address parking concerns, Mr. Shivakumar said the Metro authority has been directed to acquire an additional three to four acres near each station. “They can build commercial spaces above and parking below,” he added.

title: Former MLA slams govt for not providing irrigation water in Pangal mandal
summary: Former Kollapur MLA criticizes Congress government for failing to provide irrigation water to farmers in Pangal mandal.
content:
Former Kollapur MLA Beeram Harshavardhan Reddy has alleged that the Congress government had failed to provide irrigation water to farmers in Pangal mandal despite the Jurala project being brimming with water.
During an inspection of the MJ4, D8, D18, and 19 canals in Davajipalli and Rainipalli villages in the Pangal mandal on Tuesday, the BRS leader has slammed the State government for allegedly neglecting the farmers’ needs, contrasting it with the previous government’s efforts under K. Chandrashekar Rao’s leadership.
The former MLA highlighted the issues plaguing the canals, including tree growth and debris, which obstruct water flow. He recalled the previous government’s initiatives, including the construction of checkdams and provision of compensation to farmers.
Mr. Reddy warned that if the issue is not resolved, the farmers will hold a dharna programme. He urged the District Collector to take the initiative to provide water to the farmers, accusing public representatives of neglecting their responsibilities.

title: Rythu Sangham condemns arrest of union leaders in Karedu village
summary: The Andhra Pradesh Rythu Sangham has strongly condemned the ‘arbitrary’ arrest of farmers’ and agricultural workers’ union leaders at Karedu village in Nellore district.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh Rythu Sangham has strongly condemned the ‘arbitrary’ arrest of farmers’ and agricultural workers’ union leaders at Karedu village in Nellore district.
A.P. Rythu Sangham president V. Krishnaiah and General Secretary K. Prabhakar Reddy in a statement on Tuesday (August 5, 2025) said that Mooli Vengayya (District Secretary, A.P. Rythu Sangham), Mangala Pullayya (District Secretary, A.P. Agricultural Workers Union), and Kumar (CITU leader) were detained by Ulavapadu police under the pretext of Section 30 when they attempted to visit Karedu.
The leaders termed the arrests an undemocratic and oppressive act, questioning the government’s decision to ban people’s representatives from entering the village.
Blaming the State government, they said that Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu is afraid of people’s movements. The arrests are an attempt to suppress public dissent and hide the government’s forced land allocation to IndoSol Solar, a subsidiary of Shirdi Sai Group, against the will of local farmers.
“This is a ploy to stifle the voice of thousands of farmers and agricultural workers who are openly protesting the coercive land acquisition. But repression through police force cannot silence people’s resistance,” they added.

title: Congress dividing people in the name of caste and religion: BJP
summary: Telangana BJP president warns against Congress dividing people, criticizes government's failures, and announces national flag hoisting program.
content:
Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao has cautioned the people about the ruling Congress which is ‘dividing people in terms of castes and communities and has conveniently buried the guarantees given before the elections to various sections of the society’.
“Not only farmers but every section of the society, including women, youth, students, employees and pensioners, are suffering under the Congress rule. If it was a corrupt BRS rule earlier, we have a government now which is anti-people,” he charged on Tuesday.
Addressing a district level party workers meeting at Peddapalli during his ongoing tour, Mr. Rao said the time has come for people to choose a nationalist party like the BJP which has been expanding steadily in the State. He warned the people about the ‘deceitful’ tactics of Congress which is trying to cheat Backward Class communities again with 42% reservations while including 10% quota for Muslims in it.
“This cannot be accepted by our party which has always opposed religion-based reservations. We are against the BC quota getting reduced to 32% reservations,” he said. The Chief Minister is well aware of the facts that his government is unable to implement 42% reservations to BCs and blaming the Centre for his failure and inefficiency.
The BJP chief has once again charged the Revanth Reddy government of not properly monitoring the sale of fertilizers and allowing black marketing leading to shortfall in availability despite the Central government providing more than sufficient quantity for the current agriculture season of about 6.14 lakh metric tonnes when the demand is 6.12 lakh metric tonnes.
“It is total failure of the State government as no other State has been experiencing any such shortfall. The agriculture department’s lackadaisical attitude in controlling the black marketers has led to the situation where the blame is being sought to be shifted onto the Centre for the shortage though the latter has been providing subsidy worth thousands of crores. The government is playing with the lives of farmers,” he maintained.
Meanwhile, party vice president G. Manohar Reddy has announced that a national flag hoisting in every house programme will be held from August 9 to August 16 where the party cadre will take out rallies hailing the role of the armed forces in ‘Operation Sindoor’, pay homage to the martyrs, felicitate veteran soldiers, hold photo exhibitions and will distribute the tricolour to households.

title: KCHR’s ‘Cosmos Malabaricus Summer School’ from August 11
summary: Explore Malabar's history with KCHR and Leiden University at Cosmos Malabaricus Summer School in Fort Kochi.
content:
The Kerala Council for Historical Research (KCHR) will organise the ‘Cosmos Malabaricus Summer School’ in collaboration with Leiden University here from August 11 to 14.
The event will explore Malabar’s history, heritage, and Dutch archival sources. It will be held at Gama Heritage Residency, Fort Kochi. The programme emerged from the Cosmos Malabaricus (CosMa) project, aimed at decoding, translating, and contextualising Dutch archival materials related to 17th–18th century Kerala, according to a release.
Noted scholars such as Jos Gommans, Lennart Bes, Lekshmi Subramanyam, and Mahmood Kooria will lead thematic sessions. The event will also host discussions on Dutch language learning and the challenges and opportunities in translating primary sources. The programme will feature archival workshops, cartographic field work, and academic and heritage roundtable sessions, it said.

title: Suicide of VFPCK employee; Controversy over non-payment of wife’s salary rages further
summary: The controversy over the suicide of V.T. Shijo,  allegedly over the prolonged delay in disbursing his wife’s salary,  deepened further on Tuesday with both the school authorities and the Education Department trading  blame.
content:
The controversy over the suicide of V.T. Shijo,  allegedly over the prolonged delay in disbursing his wife’s salary,  deepened further on Tuesday with both the school authorities and the Education Department trading  blame.
George Joseph, manager of St. Joseph’s High School in Naranamuzhi where Shijo’s wife, Lekha, is employed, said here on Tuesday that he had repeatedly taken up the matter with the District Education Office (DEO), even personally accompanying the family to resolve the issue. Despite submitting all the necessary documents long ago, he alleged that officials deliberately withheld the files.
“Even after the Education Minister’s intervention and a clear High Court directive, the officials remained unmoved. Each time, they cited lack of proper authentication as an excuse to stall the disbursement,” Mr. Joseph said.
He blamed the delay on bureaucratic red tape within the Education department and alleged that even appeals from the Minister’s office were ignored, despite the family’s long-standing ties with the CPI(M).
Lekha joined the school in 2012, but her salary had been withheld for years due to a legal dispute involving another claimant to her position. Although the High Court ruled in her favor and ordered that her salary and benefits for the past 14 years be paid, the direction is yet to be executed.
Following the suicide, three officials from the Pathanamthitta DEO have been suspended pending a departmental inquiry. They have been identified as N.G. Anilkumar (PA to the DEO), S. Firoz (Superintendent) and R. Bini (Section Clerk). However, Shijo’s family has indicated that further legal action will be initiated, asserting that mere suspensions are not enough and holding the department’s negligence responsible for his death.
DEO officials have already denied the allegations, stating that it was the school’s duty to generate the arrears bill. Officials also claimed that Lekha began receiving regular salary payments from February 2025, including the most recent payment for July.
Education Minister V. Sivankutty has intervened in the issue and assured stringent action against those found responsible for the lapse that allegedly led to Shijo’s death.
Officials have now collected a fresh application from the school, citing incomplete documentation as a reason for the continued delay. Shijo, who worked as a field staff member with the Vegetable and Fruit Promotion Council Keralam (VFPCK), was found hanging in the Moongampara forest on Sunday evening.
According to family members, Shijo was under immense financial strain after failing to arrange the fee required for his son’s admission to an engineering college in Erode, Tamil Nadu

title: Bevco opens its first super premium outlet in Thrissur
summary: Bevco opens first super premium outlet in Thrissur with wide liquor selection, air-conditioning, and beer vending machine.
content:
The first super premium outlet of the Kerala State Beverages Corporation (Bevco) opened in Thrissur on Tuesday (August 5, 2025). Harshita Attaluri, chairperson and managing director of Bevco, inaugurated the outlet at Manorama Junction. The super premium outlet spread over an area of 5,000 square metres has stocked a wide variety of liquor brands. Attached to the outlet is a godown which has the capacity to store over one lakh liquor bottles.
Ten well-trained staff members have been appointed to ensure prompt service to the customers. The super premium outlet is the first fully air-conditioned retail outlet of Bevco in the State. The outlet also has a beer vending machine. Bevco plans to open similar modern liquor outlets in Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam and Kozhikode.

title: P4 is not a scheme, but a movement, says Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu
summary: P4 is not a scheme, but a movement, says Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu. The initiative that blends welfare with empowerment is a mission of humanity, wherein people become partners of change, says the Chief Minister. He lauds a sanitary worker from Avanigadda for extending support to a poor, elderly woman.
content:
Andhra Pradesh’s flagship ‘P4 – Zero Poverty’ initiative will be rolled out across the State from August 19, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has announced, reaffirming his commitment to eradicating poverty by 2029.
Describing the programme as a transformative movement that blends welfare with empowerment, Mr. Naidu, while addressing a videoconference on Tuesday, said P4 (Public-Private-People-Partnership) aimed at bringing lasting change through collective community participation.
“It is not about welfare scheme but about ensuring emotional, social, and economic support to the vulnerable families,” Mr. Naidu said, adding that the model would become an example for the rest of the country.
Lauding sanitation worker Pallakunta Hemalatha from Avanigadda for voluntarily supporting a poor elderly woman, Mr. Naidu highlighted how individuals from humble backgrounds were becoming Margadarsis — mentors who guide and uplift Bangaru Kutumbalu (beneficiaries).
